As I was saying, my power is unbelievably straightforward. I can manipulate time. At will, I can rewind, fast-forward, stop or slow down time. It can be a few seconds or several hours - there’s no limit to how far I can go.

Now, before you get carried away, I should clarify. I can only manipulate time but I don't possess the power to erase or alter events. I can't change what has taken place. For instance, if I rewind time for a vase that has shattered, the vase goes back to its intact state before the breakage. But I can't prevent it from shattering in the first place.

Pausing time gives me a chance to halt everything around me; all sounds, movement, everything. It can be a tad bit eerie but it affords me the benefit of reflection and foresight. Let's say, in a situation that needs quick thinking or in a life-changing decision.

On the other hand, fast-forwarding is almost like skipping parts of a movie, but I tend to avoid this as much as possible. You understand, life is about enjoying every moment, right?

All in all, it's a power that has its uses but doesn’t undermine the normal course of life. It's like having an unusual control of time, nothing more than that.

The demon offered help with a sinister grin, "Just let me in, and let the success begin!” It enticed the poor Rudolf, with glistening eyes, “With my power, you could even guide Santa's skies!"

Rudolf was tempted; it was a tempting offer indeed, To be accepted, treated as an equal and freed, He thought to himself, "This is just what I need!" Unsure though, he asked, "How do I proceed?"

"Only ask," the demon smirked wide, "And all the power you crave will be provided, Just promise in return, a year of your life," It wasn’t much but caused a twinge of strife.

While Rudolf pondered this pact he might make, A small voice piped up, causing him to awake, It was the smallest elf, named Jingle Bell, With wide, earnest eyes and tears that fell.

"Rudolf, don't listen!" Jingle cried, "This demon is tricking you, it surreptitiously lied, There's always another way, a path untried, Believe in your own strength, let that be your guide."

The demon chuckled, "What would an elf know?" But Jingle Bell bravely countered the blow, "I know about love, friendship, and snow, And I know real power comes from the courage we show."

Listening closely, Rudolf found his resolve, The demonic temptation began to dissolve, “I’ll take my chances, my problems to solve,” He addressed the demon, his voice sounding brave and bold. 

With a howl of disgust, the demon vanished, Its cruel intentions quelled and banished, Rudolf felt the heaviness in his heart diminished, Standing tall, fear and anxiety vanished.

With newfound courage, Rudolf returned, When Christmastime came, in the lead, he was affirmed, Underneath his nose, the red light seemed to burn brighter, Guiding Santa’s sleigh, none could be a better fighter.

In the end, Rudolf had learned and grown, Proving to himself, his worth was his own, Even in darkness, his light had shone, He didn't need a demon; his strength was alone.

At first, when I realized I had powers during The Awakening, it was exciting. Everyone was discovering their strange new capabilities, and it felt like an era of comic books come to life. Some people developed super speed, others invisibility. I knew a guy who could read thoughts, and a girl who could manipulate fire. A superhero society was born overnight.

It was a whirlwind of chaos and excitement, and in the middle of it all, I was eager to discover my power. Maybe I could fly or create ice from thin air. But when my turn came, my power was...less impressive.

I can make things slightly damp. Not soaking wet, not even really wet, just mildly damp. Socks, papers, food... whatever I want, really. There’s no natural disaster I can prevent, no criminal I can defend against. It's as mild as powers can get.

At first, it was disheartening; frustrating even. I was the butt of countless jokes, the poster boy for useless powers. I felt left out, insignificant in a world now dominated by superheroes. But as I continued living with my dud power, I realized... it's not so bad.

Having a dud power meant I didn't have the weight of responsibility the real superheroes had. I couldn't read minds, so I wasn't burdened with secrets. I couldn’t control weather, so I wasn't blamed for unintended storms. I wasn't savagely fighting villains or dealing with public scrutiny. Being ordinary in an extraordinary world has its perks.

It also meant I got to remain a spectator, observing the world's new, dynamic theater. While others were busy saving the day, I had time to enjoy life, to fall in love, to watch movies and read books without interruption from some crisis.

Maybe the world sees my power as a dud, but to me, it’s a blessing in disguise. It's kept me grounded. It's kept me human in a world turning superhuman.

So, for any others out there feeling down about their ‘dud’ powers, cheer up. There's more to life than being super. Besides, there’s something satisfying about making your coffee the perfect drinking temperature or ensuring your clothes are pre-steamed. Trust me, it’s not so bad having a dud power.

Imagine you're in a field. Green extends in all directions, a vibrant quilt of varying hues. The lush blades of grass harmoniously sway with the soft whisper of the wind, carrying along the scent of the earth- a simple, yet profound, testament to life.

Far out to the side, you can see a marginal line of forest, old trees standing tall, their majestic silhouettes cutting through the cerulean sky. Gently sprawling hills rise in the distance, adding waves to the green ocean-like expanse of the field.

The sky above is clear blue and infinite, dotted with soft cotton candy clouds casting ever-changing shapes and shadows on the ground. The sun is high in the sky, its beams painting golden streaks, creating a beautiful contrast with the verdant scenery.

The tranquility of the vastness envelops you, imprisons any worry that attempts to surface, pushing it back into the recesses of your subconscious. The world is reduced to this moment, rendering everything else meaningless and far away.

An odd butterfly with flamboyantly coloured wings makes a lazy approach, twirling and skimming close to the yellow dandelions that burst forth here and there. Their vibrant yellow is a beautiful juxtaposition to the uniform emerald.

In the distance, you hear the playful babble of a stream, it’s voice muffled by the wind that carries it to you. A flock of birds ascends in a synchronized dance, dotting the indigo sky with their small silhouettes, their chirping a harmonious symphony that compliments the quiet rustling of the leaves.

On the edge of your vision, a lone tree stands. It is colossal, an ancient sentinel. Its branches wide and welcoming. Beneath its shade, you can see a weather-worn wooden bench. It's an invitation, a promise of rest and silent companionship.

As you walk through this painting-like spectacle, a feeling of tranquility washes over you. Every step, every breath you take somehow seems fuller, easier. A sense of profound peace permeates your being, whispering in your ear the simple truth – that you belong here, in this timeless green sanctuary. That it isn't merely a place outside, but within. A part of you, a part of your soul.

Far from the cacophony of the world, ensconced in this sea of green, you realize this isn’t just a field - it's a memory, a feeling, a universe unto itself. A page in the endless book of existence, and for these divine moments you're in it, you're the text that gives it meaning and vitality.

But sometimes, it wasn't as straightforward as it seemed. Things were often shrouded in shades of gray. The right path wasn't always the easiest one. It often meant making difficult decisions, sacrifices, and sometimes, facing the scorn of others. 

There was an instance when I was working in a big corporation. I stumbled across a corrupt practice where senior officials were siphoning off funds for their personal use. It was a dire situation. The supposedly 'right thing' would have been to keep quiet and bury this secret like everyone else, but my conscience would not permit it.

So, with a racing heart and a fervent hope for justice, I reported the problem to the company's ethics committee. 

The subsequent weeks were mired in office politics, animosity, and retaliation. But I withstood it all and held firmly to my belief. In the end, the culprits were ousted, and reforms were made to prevent such abuses in the future. 

However, my journey was not straightforward post that incident. My colleagues distrusted me, bosses viewed me with suspicion and I was sidelined in projects. It cost me my peace, a fair few friends and for a time, it felt like it cost me my career too. 

But, I would do it again. Because it was the right thing. Not every battle results in immediate glory and not every right action fetches applause. But at the end of the day, when I lay my head on the pillow, I sleep knowing I had been true to my principles, trying to make the world a smidgen better. 

Being right may not always be easy or comfortable. It may lead you down a lonely road. But it will give you the solace and the strength to face yourself in the mirror every day. That, to me, is the essence of trying to do the right thing.

The beast was finally down, his grotesque figure sprawled across the cracked pavement, his monstrous reign brutally ended. The creature's bulbous eyes began to fade, that fierce yet dreadful glow sifting into an abyssal darkness. Liam's hand was trembling as he looked at his sword, smeared with thick scarlet liquid that was once pulsating through the veins of the vanquished monster.

He slowly backtracked, his combat boots scraping along the gravel, leaving a rickety trail behind. His breath was ragged and the wind that heated his cheek on this moonlit night felt like a sharp sting.

Liam glanced around at the desolate scene. The once bustling city now lay in ruins, cast into eerie shadows by the ghostly pallor of the moon. Desecrated buildings, burnt vehicles and no sounds but the occasional rustling of leaves and the hollow echo of his own footfall. The only remnants of civilization were the splattered crimson, the crumbled stone, and the oppressive silence, so profound it was as if the city itself were holding its breath.

Swallowing hard, he tried to steady his hands, the sword shaking in an unknown rhythm of fear and relief. His breath fogging up in the chilled night, he leaned against the remains of a desolate wall, trying to calm the riotous thumping in his chest.

A sense of relief washed over Liam. The oppressive aura that seemed to hang over the city was beginning to lift. The monster was no more, its reign of terror ended. But this relief was tainted with a bittersweet taste, for he remembered the lives it had devoured, turning what was once a flourishing city into a ghost town.

Taking one last glance at the beast's corpse, Liam started off towards his shelter. The journey was long and tiresome, but the weight on his shoulders lessened with each step. He had avenged his people, ended the cruel chapter that had scarred the city. But at what cost? The empty streets were a poignant testament to the price they had all paid.

As Liam trudged off into the night, disappearing into the labyrinth of decimated buildings and narrow alleyways, the once fearsome beast remained, a grotesque monument to a city's torment and eventual survival. The blood continued to trickle down its remains, hitting the floor in a rhythmic, yet eerie tone echoing out in the cold silence of the night.

Sonuva James was not a man who gave much thought to fear. He had faced down more than his fair share of danger, both in the saloons and the wilds of the frontier. His old bones were permanently etched with tales of adventure, his skin weathered by relentless sun.

The chilling scream that echoed through the still night was familiar - a signal from the outpost tower, warning of incoming danger. He had heard it many times before. But it never failed to send a shiver down his spine. Years of honing his reactions allowed Sonuva James to react in mere seconds, his calloused hands reaching for his trusted rifle that never strayed too far from reach.

The wooden door creaked in the quiet night as he swung it open, the echo spreading through the small settlement. Briefly, he paused, the night breeze brushing against his rough skin, carrying with it the distant scent of danger. Burning wood, sweat, and the hint of blood. It raised his hackles and he took a deep breath, steeling himself for what was to come.

His eyes, honed by years living in uncivilized lands, quickly adjusted to the darkness, scanning the expanse before him for signs of movement. The imposing silhouette of the outpost tower stood against the moonlit sky, an ominous figure that spurred him into action.

Sonuva James didn't hesitate. Rifle firmly in hand, he kicked the dirt beneath his boots and made for the tower, a fierce determination etched on his lined face. He wasn't sure what awaited him, but he had declared a silent oath to protect his people. And he'd be damned if he'd let anything or anyone break that vow.

The hardness in his features pronounced his resolve, his lips hitched upward into a grim smile. The shout of the wind and the distant cries were a brutal symphony, setting the rhythm for his quick stride, a heartbeat against the silence of the frontier night. There was a battle to be fought. And Sonuva James would fight it till his very last breath. Because that’s what he did. That's who he was. The guardian of his people, a legend in his own right.

Curiosity piqued and irritation flaring, he approached the peculiar site, each step crunching rhythmically on the lush spring grass. He knew his wife held occasional moonlit soirees with her mystical-minded weaving society, but he never expected to see such blatant signs of their activities.

He noticed tiny symbols etched into the ground at the center of each circle. This further piqued his interest as these weren’t just any ordinary ash circles; these held a significance he couldn't understand.

Just as his fingertips dusted off one of the intricate symbols, a single gust of wind whooshed by, sending the ash aloft in a cloud of silvery specks. Stuttering on a handful of exasperated expletives, he squeezed his eyes shut, coughing at the unexpected grit.

After regaining his composure, Mr. Jones straightened and looked around, half-expecting to see his wife's weaving society women pop out from behind the manicured hedges, wrapped in their colorful shawls and suppressing giggles with hennaed hands. He turned to walk back inside when he noticed tiny footprints leading away from the ash circles, beckoning him to follow. A smile tugged at his lips. Although often preceded by strange phenomena like unseasonal weather or peculiar celestial alignments, his arrival never heralds much. Each time, he appears without fanfare, a smoky apparition evolving to a tangible form in the blink of an eye. Typically, he adorns the same form, a tall and lean figure with obsidian eyes that seem to absorb all light. His skin carries an ethereal glow, a radiant silver that seems to shimmer in twilight.

He rarely interacts with his surroundings, preferring to silently witness the goings-on of the world. Occasionally, he would intervene in situations that piqued his interest, effortlessly resolving what to mortals appeared as insurmountable problems.

Strangely enough, despite his aloof and dispassionate demeanor, there is aetherial kindness about him, as he always strives to keep collateral damage to a minimum, engaging in battles away from human habitation when confronted by entities of his caliber.

On rare occasions, his silent vigil was punctuated by brief conversations with those brave or foolhardy enough to approach him. His speech was always cryptic, full of riddles and complex metaphors, yet those who managed to decipher his words swear they gained wisdom they'd carry to their graves.

And then, just as mysteriously as he arrived, he would disappear without a word, an ephemeral wisp fading away, leaving behind the faintest aroma of ozone and a lingering feeling of awe. His absences would often span years, decades, or even centuries, but the certainty of his return was as constant as the cycles of the sun and the moon. He was an enigma, a cryptic presence in the world of mortals, his existence interwoven with the earth's truest mysteries.

Still, his visits, despite being infrequent, were etched into the collective memory of humanity. Tales of his appearances turned into legends, then myths, and finally seeped into every part of the culture, permeating art, literature, and even religious texts. 

In every culture and every civilization, he existed in some shape or form; a testament to his bewildering, yet captivating relationship with the affairs of the mortal realm. In each rendition of the tales, he was hailed as a silent guardian, a powerful wanderer, a celestial soothsayer—always observant, always vigilant, always ready to surface during times of greatest need. His importance could not be overstated, and yet, even with the plethora of evidence of his interactions with our world, his true purpose remained shrouded in mystery. Who he truly was, why he made his sporadic appearances, and where he was when absent from our realm, were burning questions, unsolved puzzles that fascinated and frustrated scholars and historians through ages.  

But regardless of these unknowns, one thing seemed to at least remain constant. No matter how brief, no matter how insignificantly small his appearances seemed, they always, without exception, brought about profound changes—ones that would ripple through the ages, shaping the course of history and the destiny of the entire humankind.

He let out an exasperated sigh and leaned back on the couch, his patience running thin. It had been almost 10 minutes now and the buffering icon was still circling on the screen enigmatically. Pulling out his phone, Shelton quickly googled "how to speed up internet connection". The search engine provided various suggestions like resetting the WiFi router, clearing the cache, and finally, moving the router to a different location for better signal strength. 

Scrolling through the list, he decided to try the easiest solution first. He stood up, headed towards the small closet where the router was tucked away. The small blinking lights, green, yellow, red, were like the city skyline at night. He held his breath, hoping that resetting the router would be enough to get his tablet back up and running.

After a moment of hesitation, he finally pushed the small black button on the back of the router. The blinking lights shut off for a moment and then started flashing vigorously. "Alright," Shelton thought, "let's hope this helps."

Back on the couch, he picked up the tablet again, refreshed the page, and waited with bated breath. After a few agonizingly slow loading moments, the stream suddenly came on. He let out a sigh of relief as the sound of music filled his quiet living room.

One day, it was just a small, seemingly ordinary potted plant placed on the windowsill. It had tiny, luscious green leaves and minor buds ready to bloom any day. We’d thought it was sweet, innocuous, and perfect for brightening up our office.

Every morning, we’d water it and take a moment to admire the promise of life it represented. As weeks turned into months, we began to notice it growing at a surprisingly rapid pace. Initially, we laughed it off, attributing it to our excellent gardening skills. It grew taller, its leaves spread wider and bigger, creating a canopy of deep green in an otherwise drab environment.

One day, we came to the office to find it stretching towards the ceiling, the plant's once small buds bursting with oversized, vibrant flowers. It had grown larger than the tallest man in our office, much to our surprise. Its tendrils curled perfectly around office cubicles, somehow not causing any disruption but subtly becoming a very present entity in our workspace.

Nobody could explain it. The plant seemed to thrive, appearing healthier and more vibrant every day. Soon, its creeping vines began to envelop our desks, its large leaves often casting shadows on our computer screens. Its fragrance filled up our office, a mélange of peculiar, intoxicating floral scents. It was all amusing in a peculiar way until the plant got so large it began to cause problems.

It was on a Thursday when we realized that the plant—our plant—had taken over half of the office space. Its roots had invaded the walls, piercing through the concrete, the ceiling was obscured by a thick canopy of broad leaves, and the floor was a matrix of coiled tendrines. That morning, we all stood outside the office building, the expressions of bewilderment mirrored on our faces.

We tried to call in professionals, botanists, gardeners, even a paranormal investigator—no one could explain the phenomena. The mystery of our plant grew along with its roots, leaves, flowers, and stems.

It was a spectacle that was not missed by the city. Newspapers started writing about "the plant office," TV reporters camped outside our building trying to get a scoop. We became celebrities of some sort. Tours were arranged, scientists flocked to study it, and we somehow embraced the adoration until one of us suggested an idea.

Maybe this plant was showing us how nature could retake places consumed by our corporate world. Perhaps, it was nature's way of reclaiming the space we humans had unwittingly usurped. 

And so, we adapted. Workstations were set up within the green maze, the rustling leaves, and sweet scents becoming a soothing background to our regular workdays. Friendships bloomed amidst its branches, and the plant, our plant, remained an equal, an ally, teaching us all a profound lesson in coexistence. 

And thus, our story continues. A story of an office, a plant, and a harmony found in the most unusual, delightful way. We still don't remember how the thing got so big, but we sure are grateful it did, for we learned to thrive along with it.

My heart beats rapidly as my fingers brush over the heavy stock paper, the resonance of authority emanating from the file, demanding caution. The words "CLASSIFIED" and "TOP SECRET" seemingly echo in my head, notes of urgency, whispering the weight and gravity of the situation.

Taking a deep breath, I glance at him, Agent Reynolds. His stoic face portrays a calmness I wish I could share, his eyes—steely grey, unyielding—never leave mine, an evident indication of the seriousness of whatever is contained within.

Swallowing, I slowly pull open the file, the faint rustle the only sound breaking the tense silence in the covert, dimly lit room.

The stark black and white of the first photo hit me like a punch, cold, unforgiving. A satellite image. It's a suspected enemy base nestled amidst dense forest, the greenery doing little to hide its militant presence. The sight of it makes my palms sweat, the reality of what this file represents seeping in.

Flipping the image over, there's a brief description, chilling in its brevity. "Location: Undisclosed. Purpose: Hostile. Save the preliminary data for operation Ghost."

Operation Ghost. The name itself leaves a chill down my spine.

As I sift through the further pages, they reveal layouts of the base, aerial views, and even profiles of known associates tied to the installation. Each person's photo feels like a gaze into the abyss, their black and white stills holding an eerie quiet, silently screaming their roles in a narrative of criminality.

The last sheet is a mission outline, my mission. It's straightforward but far from simple - infiltrate the base, gather enough evidence to confirm its purpose, get out unnoticed. Terms of engagement: Silent.

Handing the file back to the agent, I feel the weight lifting from my hands but not off my shoulders. I stand and shake Agent Reynolds' hand. His grip is firm, unyielding, just like his gaze. 

"Good luck," He says, his voice as hard as the stone walls surrounding us.

Little did I know, luck was something I would desperately need in the operation lying ahead. The walls of the room seemed to close on me in anticipation, holding their breath for a mission that would inevitably shatter the stillness of the unknown location nested in the file: Operation Ghost had officially begun.

Joshua, our group's ever-astonished ambassador, was pointing at what looked like a massive spider, sprawled on the side of a eucalyptus tree. His cheeks had gone pale, his hands shaking at an alarming rate, the epitome of his New Yorker persona jolting into overdrive. This innocuous suburban landscape was slowly weakling this tough city-dweller. 

"A Huntsman spider," our guide, Jason, said with a reassuring smile. He was the perfect image of the rugged, indisputable Aussie flaunting a fading, tanned skin, laid-back persona, and daunting knowledge about the wild. 

The spider was enormous, to say the least. Its fat, hairy body and long, spread-out legs made it look more like an alien than any creature that belonged on any tree in the world. It was a living embodiment of the lurid images that represented Australia's exotically terrifying fauna in Joshua's mind. 

"Oh for god's sake! Why is everything in this country trying to kill us?" Joshua exclaimed, jumping back, his face contorting in melodramatic horror. This met with hearty laughter from our group, including Jason. 

"Relax, mate. Huntsman spiders are harmless. Unless you're a bug, then you're pretty screwed," Jason explained, giving Joshua a slap on the back which did little to soothe him. 

Despite his irrational fear, this was the charm of Australia. The land down under hosted an enigmatic array of strange and diverse creatures, that was bound to shock out-of-towners like Joshua. All you needed was a rigid composure and the spirit of curiosity to appreciate the country's unique biodiversity.

For the rest of the day, we moved deeper into the wilderness, learning about kangaroos, koalas, wombats and even Tasmanian devils. Joshua's exclamations tuned down from a panicky tremor to an interested murmur. After all, it was turning out to be quite an adventure, terrifyingly large spiders included. Although he could do without them.

By nightfall, as we returned to our lodging, a peaceful lull blanketed the crew. All was quiet except for the distant chirping of a Kookaburra, serenading us to sleep. Fears gradually turned into fascination and horror into curiosity as we continued our exploration throughout the week. The Aussie wilderness had found a place in our hearts. In Joshua's words, it was "Terrifyingly beautiful!"

"She didn't let it at that, but took a deep sigh, visage full of apprehension, brows arched as if carrying the weight of the world, her lips a tight line. The dim lights of the diner we sat in suddenly felt oppressive, like a shroud slowly descending.

"I have been feeling strange of late," she continued, her gaze fixed at the empty cup of coffee on our table, but her eyes did not seem to see it, they seemed to see something beyond. The fingers of her left hand were incessantly tapping on her cup's edge. Ping. Ping. Ping. It was the only sound overlaid on our silence other than the distant murmur of other patrons in the diner.

I watched her silently, my heart pounding in my chest as uncertainty curled around me. Arielle. My Arielle, so vivacious, full of joy and dreams, now looked like a mirage that would dissolve if I touched her. It scared me.

Arielle slowly returned her gaze at me. A sad smile softened the tight lines of her face, "I took a test before I came here, Josh. It was positive. We're...I'm pregnant."

The words seared across the desert of my blank mind setting ablaze the carefully cultivated calm I had built. 'We are pregnant. We are pregnant.' The words echoed against the walls of my mind, multiplying until they turned into a cacophonous symphony.

"Are you... are you sure it's ours," I mumbled, my voice faltering under the weight of what it would mean if it were true.

A strange sort of resignation flashed through her eyes before they shuttered themselves off, making them unreadable. "Josh, there hasn't been anyone else but you in my life for the past month."

She reached out across the table, her fingers brushing against mine. It felt like an electric shock through the contact. A myriad of emotions washing over me – panic, trepidition, confusion, but also some twisted form of elation. How could two weeks lead to this? A seed of life already growing within Arielle. A being that was half her, half me.

The enormity of the situation suddenly hit me. A child. Our child. We barely knew each other. What were we supposed to do now? This wasn't how I envisioned our relationship moving forward. A relationship only two weeks old was not built to handle such an existential bombshell.

Yet, as the panic receded to be replaced with a sense of stoic acceptance, I also realized something profound – this was bigger than us. Bigger than our inconsequential plans. This was life itself, creating its own narrative.

"Alright," I found myself saying finally, giving her fingers a reassuring squeeze. "We will figure this out, Arielle. We're in this together."

Little did we know, the journey we undertook that night would not just alter our lives but shape us into completely different individuals than we were at that diner. Together, we embarked on a road, fraught with challenges and uncertainty, but also filled with the miraculous joys of a life that only 'parents' could comprehend."

"I've Bean Here Before" is not just any regular cafe. From the outside, it might look like one, with its warm, twinkling lights and rustic wooden sign. But once you step inside, you realize there's something different about this place.  

The furnishing is mismatched, bohemian, with a noticeable theme of bean-shaped pieces including lamps, tables even the wallpapers have whimsical bean patterns. But this isn't the weird part.

The weirdest part is the fact that every time I go there, it feels like I've exactly been there before - not just in the sense of physical location. The feeling is more specific, much stronger. 

For instance, as I order my usual cappuccino, I know exactly how the barista is going to react, the subtle twitch of her lips before she repeats my order, like a deja vu. When I find a corner to sit down with my book, the conversations around me don't just sound familiar, they seem to play out exactly like I remember them - word for word.

The first few times, I brushed it off, rationalizing it to be coincidences. After all, cafes do have fixed routines and regular customers. But it happened every single time, consistently. It seemed as if the cafe was stuck in a temporal loop or was it just my mind playing tricks on me? 

Despite the peculiarities, I kept going back. Maybe it was the comfort of the predictable, or the strangely addictive quality of the puzzling situation. 

The cafe is an unexplainable twilight zone in my otherwise ordinary life. It continues to baffle me yet lures me with its warmth and the delicious aroma of its coffee. Despite its odd reputation among my friends, to me, "I've Bean Here Before" is like a tranquil island amid the chaotic sea of life.

Alex had been starstruck when he saw her. Her name was Lila and she was the lead vocalist in his favorite indie band. Every time they performed, he attended without fail, hopelessly drawn to her energy, her voice, her persona. It was a kind of magic that seemed to radiate off her, captivate her audience, and keep them coming back for more.

Tonight, however, was different. He hadn't merely seen Lila perform from a distance; they'd crossed paths in a small café after the concert. The chance encounter was far from his wild imaginations of somehow meeting her backstage or in an autograph signing event.

Caught off guard by her radiant eyes meeting his, as she looked up from her steaming cup of coffee, he was a portrait of a deer caught in headlights. Alex could barely summon the courage to smile. But she did, causing his heart to beat wildly - as if marching to the rhythm of Lila's famous track, 'Runaway Heart'.

Trying to shuffle past his shyness, he mustered enough strength to approach her. He muttered a shy "Hi", followed by praise for her recent performance.

To his surprise, Lila, who must have been approached by countless fans, gave him an appreciative smile, her interest visibly picked. She gestured to the empty chair across her table, inviting him to sit. Alex's heart pounded a frantic rhythm as he took a seat, fighting to suppress his wide, starstruck grin. His idol was welcoming his company, and he was grateful that he'd mustered up just enough courage to approach her. 

For the next couple of hours, the small café became their own little world. Stars sparkled outside the window, while inside, Alex found a star in Lila who was humble, kind, and genuinely inspiring. As they shared stories and laughter, Adam realized he wasn't just starstruck anymore. He had connected with his idol on a profoundly human level and those few hours unwittingly shaped an increasing admiration for Lila - not just as a rockstar, but as a person. This was a night he would remember for the rest of his life. 

Unbeknownst to him, Lila felt a similar connection. Alex was different from the other fans; he was genuine, warm-hearted, and his admiration felt sincere and profound. She felt that they'd crossed paths for a reason and she was glad they did.

Sir Charles, that is what men called him had dedicated his entirety to the blossoming of an intriguing maze around the castle he so carefully guarded. His armor was a reflection of time and elements, aged and weathered, yet the stern expression on his heavily whiskered face suggested an unwavering spirit that defined his perseverance throughout the years.

He ogled at the garden, his eyes following the weave and weave of the neatly sculpted hedges, a marvel in themselves, dictating the directions in an unspoken language that could only be understood if you surrendered to their counterparts' invitations. The crescent pond blushed in its glory, immersed in the reflection of the twilight sky, mirroring the golden crimson hue.

The knight's cheeks reddened with anticipation and delight, his heart pounded like a young boy who just spotted his first love, he stepped on the green carpet of trimmed grass and onto the stone paved path, the soft clinks of his armor a reminder of his age and lifelong duty.

His eyes roved into the unknown abyss of the pathways, their contents hidden by the shadows of dusk; the playful chirping of the birds and the melodious whistles of the wind was the only companion he had today, apart from his trusty rusted sword. It was in these strolls where he found peace, where he was free from duty and could take off his armor, at least in his thoughts.

As he moved around the crescent pond, he noticed the last rays of sun sparkling on the calm surface, speaking to him in a language that only he understood. The age might have slowed his legs, but time only made him wiser; he was unperturbed by the length of the paths and instead was more eager for the enchanting journey that lay ahead of him.

Off he moved, choosing his path with precision that spoke of his respect for the hedges, their secrets well-guarded by him. For this old knight, the castle was not the priority, rather the maze of hedges was the treasure that he’d sworn to protect, each stroll a chapter in an unwritten book, every path a journey that led him into a world he treasured more than his loyalty towards the realm. 

And so, the knight ventured deeper, guided by the whispers of the evening, embarking once again on an expedition that had no destination, but was instead filled with the joy of discovery and the magic of the unexplored. All until the stars took over the sky, twinkling with their thousand-year stories and giving him a new excuse, a fresh reason to cherish the walks again the following evening.

The black-and-white flickering of the M*A*S*H rerun on the old television screen was the only source of light, illuminating the otherwise pitch-dark basement. I squinted in the dim light, adjusting my glasses and stiffening at the sight of motionless reflection in the corner of my vision.

In the still silence of the night, that stony placidity was near deafening. But it wasn't just that. It was also his eyes - the power they seemed to hold. Those eyes spoke stories, truths, and even the weight of emotion, wrapped in an unspoken understanding of life itself. The silver-haired actor, even on screen, had an innate charisma that was hard not to marvel at.

The episode ended, leaving his image frozen on the screen. The silent echo of warm laughter that usually followed now seemed distant and jarringly absent. Even with the annoying buzz of the television and the howling wind outside, the space felt bizarrely quiet. It was as if time held its breath, patiently waiting for the reel to spin once more.

I sat back in my worn armchair and chuckled lightly to myself, running my fingers through my unkempt hair. The faint memory of his character, Hawkeye Pierce, echoed in my mind. It was a different era then - one of social turmoil, political upheaval and a country on the brink of change. Perhaps it was that similarity that made me feel so drawn to such an iconic figure.

His laughter, his wit, his resilience, they all felt excruciatingly relatable. Suddenly, it was about more than a television show. It was about life and its incredible ability to surprise us, to amuse us and more than anything, to endure.

The digitized beep from the television brought me back to reality. The screen flickered back to life and Alan Alda was gone, replaced by a new episode, a new scene. Yet, the glance he had left etched into my mind seemed to cast a lasting echo long into the night.

Whether it was the glacial blue eyes piercing through the observation screens, or the complex layered magnetism of his off-screen persona, the seemingly distant figure of Alan Alda had managed to reach me, grounding me in the solemn, yet somehow comforting presence of a shared human experience.

Besides him on the mahogany desk, lay a half-eaten sandwich and a strong cup of coffee, now cold. Droplets of condensation formed on the window, as rain poured continuously outside. The gloomy weather seemed to echo the somber expressions on people's faces that showed up on the live feed.

What had begun as a news feature, showing footage of people mysteriously disappearing worldwide with claims that they were given suddenly divine "uplifts", had rapidly spread into a global phenomenon. The phenomenon, eerily similar to the concept of "rapture" as mentioned in religious texts, was something that humans had spent eons contemplating. Now, it was right there on his screen, impossible to ignore.

Hal was an investigative journalist, known among peers for his critical thinking prowess and stoic demeanor. But the past few days watching people abruptly vanish from existence had shaken even him. They showed no sign of pain or grief, but merely a moment of sublime peace before vanishing, leaving behind clothes in a crumpled heap. 

Every day, Hal spent hours talking to the friends and families of those who were 'taken'. Some pleaded desperately for him to find a pattern, a reason, while most were merely content to share their grievances. Even Hal's theological companion and close friend, Josh, had been taken. 

On the screen, the scenes shifted from place to place globally, showcasing bewildered crowds observing the phenomenon and praying for it to stop. The fear was palpable, with everyone dreading that they or their loved ones might be next, or worse, left behind.

But Hal wasn't entirely focused on the heart-wrenching scenes of people disappearing — he was watching for patterns. Observing the footage day in and day out, he was certain that there was a pattern to the supposedly random disappearances. There had to be more rational explanations aside from divine intervention.

So, Hal pursued the truth relentlessly, collecting data, running analysis, cross-checking theories, and discarding hundreds of them when they didn't hold up. As the world panicked around him and chaos seemed to reign, he sat stoically in his office, his mind dancing around the dilapidated semblance of logic that this situation offered. 

Day three ended with no concrete conclusion. The rapture continued, but so did Hal's resolve. Tomorrow, he decided, he would need to step out and witness the phenomenon up close. Only by braving the center of the storm can one find solutions, he thought.

In a world slowly dissolving into madness, Hal remained a flicker of hope, seeking solutions amidst chaos. And as the final news footage of the day faded out, Hal rallied on, clinging tightly to his faith in reason, and preparing for the uncertain dawn ahead.

My eyes scrutinised the intricate detail of the hand; it was far from a mere collection of bones, tendons, and muscles covered with a layer of skin. It was more like a masterpiece stained in crimson; the skeletal structure burdened with the duties of picking up fine grains of salt, writing sonnets and caressing a loved one, and at the same time, capable of crushing a jugular.

A thin layer of icy fear pricked my skin, sending a shiver down my spine. I repressively tried to swallow the lump of anxiety forming in my throat, as I turned my gaze back towards her. 

Her face bore a calm generosity, her lips playing a sweet symphony that would lure any sensible man into her snare. Her eyes, however, held a different story, one of power, dominance, and an insatiable craving for something beyond the grasp of normality. They twinkled menacingly under the soft glow of the chandelier, like two far-off galaxies enveloped in a mystical shroud of secrets.

She subtly tilted her head and her lips stretched into a sardonic grin, revealing a set of teeth as pristine as ivory. I could only offer her a dutiful, albeit uneasy, nod in return. My mind was swimming in a sea of confusion, a possible death sentence clashing with the alluring beauty in front of me.

"I have chosen you," she spoke. Her voice was like the calming hush of a gentle ocean tide, but its undercurrent sent waves of unease pulsating through me.

To be chosen would mean, in the best-case scenario, to become a part of this endless dance between the hunter and the hunted. It could also mean - my mind recoiled from the thought – to serve as her intellectual distraction until she tired of me.

One thing was certain, though - I was now bound in the intricate, deadly web of a creature wearing the mask of beauty, one that wielded power and terror with an uncanny ease, making me a puppet in her world of chaos. The night was indeed young and full of terrors!

The man cleared his throat nervously before he continued, avoiding Thorn’s piercing gaze. "You see sir," he started, his voice barely above a whisper, "The village...it's in ruins."

Thorn’s frown deepened, his dark eyes narrowing at the man’s words. "Ruins?" he repeated, standing from his chair with unexpected feline grace, "What do you mean, ruins?"

The man flinched and took a step back as Thorn towered over him. Even sitting, Thorn was intimidating, but standing made the stark reality of his stature and power almost unbearable to look at. Even though he was trim and lean, there was a certain solidness to him. His shoulders were broad, his arms muscular. His whole persona emanated menace.

"I-I meant what I said, sir," the man stammered, his hands clenching and unclenching at his sides. "The Lancasters, they… they attacked."

Thorn’s expression remained unreadable. The man saw no surprise, no shock - only a sinister calmness. He felt a shiver crawl up his spine as he waited for Thorn to respond.

"And?" Thorn finally said after a long, unbearable silence prodding the man to say more.

"They've taken everyone captive, sir. Women, children...everyone. They set the houses on fire, and...and..." He swallowed thickly, the image of his once peaceful village in ashes haunting his every blink.

Thorn was quiet for what felt like an eternity, his face like cold, hard stone. Then, his lips pulled into a tight, grim line. "Prepare the horses," he commanded, his voice as cold as winter winds, "We're going to pay the Lancasters a visit."

I had been trawling through the thick, dusty volumes all day, my fingers leaving trails on the aged paper, yet I was no closer to finding what I was looking for. The library was my sanctuary, a place where time seemed to hang still and lose its essence. A place where I was supposed to find answers, not an uphill struggle. But I was getting increasingly frustrated. My eyes were tired, blurred from squinting at the faded texts.

A soft, muffled tick-tock echoed through the vaulted ceiling of the room, a lone sentinel of time in this place where minutes melded into hours seamlessly. The only light came from a dim lamp on my mahogany desk, its yellow hue painting half-read books and scribbled notes with patches of shadows.

The librarian had long departed, leaving me alone with the whispering silence. A silence I usually welcomed, but tonight, it seemed too loud, almost menacing. My fingers tapped against the polished wood, matching the rhythm of the grandfather clock nestled someplace out of sight.

I rolled my neck, attempting to assuage the stiffness that had set in. Taking a deep breath, I decided to collect myself, to push away the shroud of impatience and focus on my task. I stood up, my tired legs protesting. Walking over to the ornate windows, I peered into the streets. 

The town was quiet, its inhabitants locked away in slumber. There was a certain calmness to it all, the hushed tranquility echoing that of the library. It was a stark contrast to my turbulent thoughts. Wrapping my arms around myself, I drew comfort from my own warmth. The chill from the window seeped into my skin, forming goosebumps.

Drawing the curtains back, I made my way back to the desk. The chair creaked under my weight as I sank down. Refocusing, I let my fingers glide over the pages. They whisper under the faint touch before I turn them carefully, fearful of hurting them.

Then, it was there. The information I had been so desperately seeking. A spark of triumph lit up my eyes as I traced over the familiar words, translating them in my mind. My heart pounded in my chest, the information spurring a series of thoughts and possibilities.

With a newfound energy, I got up, leaving the library behind in its slumber. The moonlight guiding my way, I was ready to face the quiet world outside, poised for a whirlwind of an adventure. The restless anticipation lingered, yes, but now it was tinged with the promise of discovery, not despair of the quest.

Inside the grocery store, I feel like shit. The fluorescent lights flicker above me, causing an uncomfortable rhythm in my brain. The overwhelming smell of the produce section makes my stomach churn and I wrap my arms around myself, trying to hold the feeling at bay. 

Despite the bustling activity around me, I feel a wall building up between me and the world. A slight haze blurs my vision of the crisp apples, the perfectly placed boxes of cereal and the vibrant array of flowers at the entrance, like I'm looking at everything through a dirty window.

I drag myself through each aisle, my mind a chaotic swirl of thoughts as I put one foot in front of the other, robotic in my movements. The chill of the frozen foods section makes me shiver, but the discomfort feels fitting.

The sound of shoppers chattering, the beeping of items being scanned, even the soft notes of the overhead music, all of it feels too loud, too intrusive. I pick up a can of soup, but my appetite is gone, lost somewhere between the bread aisle and the dairy section.

I shuffle up to the checkout line, clutching a few random items I don't really want. The cashier smiles at me, unaware of the turmoil inside me, and I do my best to return the gesture. But my smile feels fake, forced.

Outside, the afternoon sun hits my face, a stark contrast to the cold, artificial lighting inside. I sit in my car, watching people pass by in the rearview mirror, lost in their own worlds. I take a deep breath, trying to shake off the malaise, hoping tomorrow will be better. 

But for today, inside the grocery store and even out, I feel like shit.

The world powers, particularly Russia and the United States, had since the Cold War, been engaged in a clandestine battlefield, Africa. A continent rich with resources and strategical importance. They were manipulating conflicts, banking on simmering regional tensions, feeding on old rivalries and ethnic divisions. They wielded the weapon of political influence and economic assistance to gain control over a vast land that was not their own, fostering a subtle yet dire form of colonization.

Alliances were woven, and governments were propped up or taken down based on their readiness to fall in line. These puppet regimes were more interested in personal gain and the power to retain their status than the welfare of their own people. The African people bore the brunt of their leaders' greed, facing rampant corruption, civil unrest, poverty, and racial discord.

Meanwhile, arms dealers from the powerhouses gained a burgeoning market for their weapons, selling to both sides of conflicts that often had roots in the artificial divisions created by the colonizers. The sad irony lay in the fact that these were the same nations that preached peace during the day, and at nightfall, they stoked the fires of war.

However, as the decades unfolded, a shift became palpable in the strategic landscape. African nations began to wrest power from their overlords, carving alliances among themselves, guided by a shared history of exploitation, and the realization that unity was their true strength. The Organization of African Unity, and later the African Union, stood testament to this.

The machinations of the world powers faced stiff resistance, culminating in African voices collectively raised against foreign influence. The powerhouses too, dealing with their own economic crunches and escalating tensions at home, had to step back, though not entirely. Their interference had lessened, but not ended.

In the wake of this new era, Africa began to evade the shadows of the pawn piece, boldly asserting its growth and potential. Yet, the scars of the past ran deep, and countless individuals continued to pay the price for the proxy wars fought on their land.

With each passing day, the struggle for Africa waged on, a contest between the whims of the world powers and the will of a continent. It was no longer just about resources or strategic significance but the self-determination of a multitude of nations and the shared dignity of the African people. The world was watching, but this time, so too were the Africans, vigilant and unwavering in their pursuit for sovereignty.

The first door, carved with symbols of ancient knowledge, opened for a day of learning and discovery. Here, you could spend hours reading, discussing, perhaps even teaching. 

The second door, made of smooth, carved wood, led to a day of calm and relaxation. Here, you could snothe stresses of life fade away as you indulged in tranquility, perhaps through meditation, a beautiful natural view, or a good night's sleep.

The third door, painted with dazzling colors, brought a day of creativity and personal expression. Here, you might spend hours painting, dancing, writing, or simply appreciating art in its many forms.

The fourth door was built of sturdy oak and embossed with a lion, symbolizing courage and strength. The day ahead involved challenges and trials, pushing you to show your bravery and grow as an individual.

The fifth and final door, adorned with a symbol of a hearth, led to a day of warmth and love. This day would be spent with loved ones, sharing stories, laughter and companionship. 

Each door, thus, had its unique charm and experience, waiting to be embraced. With every door that opened, came a new day; a chance to learn, relax, create, challenge and love.

It was a sweltering summer in Brooklyn, and Garet was just another kid from the block trying hard to make ends meet. As a bright and ambitious teenager, he was struggling to keep up with classes while also helping his single mother with the household expenses. He was walking the delicate tightrope of dreams and reality and sometimes, it was hard to keep his balance.

The decision wasn't an easy one. Becoming a dealer in his neighborhood meant striding on the blurred lines of morality and responsibility. It meant pushing against the social norms he'd grown up respecting. But the prospects of a better life, for him and his mom, were too enticing to be ignored.

It wasn't drugs, or illegal contraband like most might assume. No, Garet was more calculated, more risk-averse than that. He had heard that old man McCallister was clearing out his comic book store, his bad health forcing him to retire early. That was Garet's chance.

He'd always had an inkling for comic books. Their vibrantly illustrated worlds held a special allure, transporting him away from his dreary life to worlds where superheroes vanquished villains and there was always a happy ending. He'd spent countless hours between the worn-out pages of those comic books, living experiences he could never have in real life.

So, when Garet heard about McCallister's plans, he started saving every penny he could. He did multiple part-time jobs, stinted on meals, walked instead of taking the bus—anything that could save him money. 

After months of hard work, Garet had just enough to make a deal with McCallister. On a cool, autumn day, he became the proud owner of a stack of comic books, crammed in old coffee-stained cardboard boxes. To him, they weren't just comic books—they represented opportunity, a fresh start, a chance to escape the cycle of poverty.

Garet started small. Selling comic books to his classmates, then to kids from neighboring blocks. He made a social media page, offering rare and second-hand comic books at affordable rates. Drawing on his love and knowledge for the artform, he soon gained a reputation as a reliable and rare comic book dealer.

Becoming a dealer was not an easy decision. There were days when Garet questioned his choice, but every time he considered giving up, he thought about those worn-out pages, the vibrant stories, and the uncharted territories inside those covers. He remembered the look of excitement on the face of a kid owning his first Spiderman edition, or the nostalgia in the eyes of an adult reuniting with a comic from his youth. He saw his community bonding over comic books, exploding the myth that print was dead.

From the dirty alleyways of Brooklyn, Garet emerged as an unexpected champion of the comic book world. He discovered that sometimes, the line between a dealer and a hero is not as distinct as it seems.

Her silhouette was enough to confirm my suspicions. The same height, the same delicate slope to her shoulders, the same confident stride. Her hair, though different in style, had the same texture and lusters in the dim lights.

She was draped in a heavy burgundy overcoat, her body swaying slightly as she made her way towards the revolving doors of the hotel. It was the sort of luxury establishment that she used to dream about when we were young and penniless, lost in a city that was too big and too hard for two kids from a small town. 

Behind me, the city roared in its usual symphony of noise - the sounds of cars, music blasting from a nearby club, the distant wail of sirey, all forming a chaotic background symphony. But in that moment, as I watched her walk away, everything fell into a hush, the clamor of the city becoming a white noise.

I stood frozen, a mixture of surprise, longing, and regret swirling within me. A thousand words tumbled around inside my head. There were so many things I wanted to say, things I should have said back then. 

As she stepped into the building, something inside me stirred, a caged bird fluttering chaotically against the bars. The barriers of fear and indecision came crashing down and I found myself striding across the street, drawn to her like a moth to a flame.

She didn’t notice my approach, her back still turned as she stood by the hotel’s reception desk. I took a before-deep breath, steeling myself. After all these years, I was finally going to talk to her again.

But before I could reach her, she turned, letting out a startle and dropping the purse she was holding. I barely had a moment to react, stepping forward and catching it before it could touch the ground. I handed it back to her and our fingers brushed, sending a jolt of electricity through me.

It was then that I finally got to see her face again. Her eyes - those brilliantly clear blue eyes - were wide with shock, her mouth agape. Our gazes locked, and for a moment, everything fell into silence.

And that's when I knew for sure. It was her. Regardless of the time that had passed, the lives we'd lived, the paths we'd walked on, I would always know her.

There was no denying it now; the girl of my past, the love of my life was standing right in front of me. Oddly, I found a strange sense of calmness within me. Looking into her eyes gave me an oddly potent mixture of pain, longing, but mostly, relief. The long search was finally over. Now, it was time for words. True words, from the deepest corners of my heart.

The woman in front of us, donned in blood-red garments, hummed softly to herself—a sound like a funeral hymn. We were in a dimly lit room, a set that seemed to be ripped straight from a nightmarish horror flick. Stacks of old sepia books and crumpled manuscripts stacked in the corner, a couple of broken down antiques, and a thick layer of dust covering everything in sight. But the striking feature was the massive, dusty mirror resting against the bare wall, bordered by gold-leafed trimmings, giving off an eerily chilling vibe.

"We are not here to harm you," my partner whispered to me repeatedly as the woman lit black candles around us, tracing a peculiar symbol on the floor. I was caught in a trance observing the room. Scenes from horror movies flashed by. A cult meeting, a witch conducting a seance, a sacrifice to the devil. My mind was racing, connecting dots that probably weren't there to begin with.

My eyes met my partner's, a tall figure, cloaked in indifference. He had a poker face on, but I could see fear lingering in his eyes. Were we handling some rogue coven? Or was this just an eccentric client?

The woman's chant grew louder, reverberating in the room, the black candles flickered violently, casting long, dancing shadows on the wall. Suddenly, she lurched forward, her porcelain-like face inches away from mine. I could feel her icy breath against my skin as she whispered, none too gently, "Are you prepared to witness the other side?"

I looked at my partner again, feeling like I was on the verge of a breakdown. Nowhere in our job description as paranormal investigators had it mentioned anything about actually crossing dimensions or interacting with spirits firsthand, if that's what she meant by "the other side". We were supposed to find rational explanations for purportedly supernatural occurrences, not participate in them!

I was stricken with confusion and fear, yet also intrigued by the prospects of the unknown. The job had stirred a sense of adventure in me, a dangerous curiosity, and maybe that's why I whispered back, "Yes." My partner shot me a baffled look, his bewildered expression echoing in the room, mirroring my own feelings of this unanticipated detour. But sometimes, you have to meet the unknown head-on, even when it's not what you signed up for.

She smirked. And suddenly the room was spinning, faster and faster until I couldn't see anything. Was this the price I had to pay for my curiosity? Everything was a blur—the eerie mirror, the flickering candles, the worried look on my partner's face. And then, everything went pitch black...

It had formed on a rather uncanny night, three years ago. It was the first night of summer, with a heavy silence carrying the weight of the night. I was plodding around my grandfather's old estate, where even the walls seemed to hold onto the haunting scent of past times.

The estate was a labyrinth of tangled gardens, long corridors, and empty rooms filled with century-old furniture. Each corner whispering tales of the generations that had lived within its stone walls. I've always had the feeling that the estate played tricks on me, like pointing me towards one direction, then whispering me towards another.

That night was no exception. A strange occurrence, a force or entity, seemed to guide me towards the old tower, a part of the estate I seldom visited due to its state of disrepair. The cobwebs hanging heavily on the decrepit wooden staircase reminded me of forgotten stories and musty old attic rooms.

Walking up those stairs, I felt something was about to change, but I couldn't put my finger on what. On top of the staircase was a small room, a timeless place tangled between the echoes of the past and whisperings of the future.

Inside the room lay a dusty old table and on it a lone treasure, a box whose exterior was showing the wear and tear of centuries. It was wooden with strangely ornate carvings inlaid with gold. It was tempting, inviting, like a fairytale luring me into an adventure.

Curiosity gnawed away at me until I found myself reaching for the box. As my hand made contact with it, I felt a sharp sting, a pricking sensation that made me quickly retract my hand. I looked down at my wrist to find a thin line of crimson blood beading against my skin, seemingly inflicted by a hidden needle on the surface of the box.

I treated the wound the best I could, wrapping a handkerchief tightly around it. As the night wore on, a new light entered my life. From the delicate paper surface of that box, intricate symbols arose, faintly glowing with an ethereal light - a light that eerily matched the one glimmering from the wound on my wrist.

From then on, the scar never faded. Instead, it began to glow, subtly, like a silent testament to that night's odd events. Ever since that night, my life took a strange turn. It's as if the scar on my wrist had unlocked a hidden realm of uncanny mysteries and strange occurrences, a life far beyond ordinary. A life intertwined with the supernatural, the mystical, and the inexplicable. With every day that passed, I dived deeper into this enigmatic world, that scar constantly reminding me of the night it all started.

The wheel of evolution turned relentlessly, forging new species from the ashes of those extinct, painting a vibrant tableau of life. The amoeba eventually gave way to vast armies of multi-cellular organisms, unique and innumerable in appearance and function, filling every niche on this planet we call home. Among them, one species stood out, walking upright, endowed with an unprecedented level of cognitive abilities, and carrying the torch of consciousness as a beacon in the unyielding darkness of ignorance and oblivion.

This species that we identify as ourselves, Homo sapiens, embarked on a journey that would fundamentally reshape not only our own destiny but that of the planet as well. We tamed fire, invented the wheel, planted crops, built civilizations and shaped nations. In our tireless march toward progress, we invested in knowledge and technology, nurtured our culture and arts, fought wars, negotiated peace, defied stereotypes, shattered taboos and consistently pushed the boundaries of our potential to become the architects of our own fate.

Yet, amid the euphoria of these phenomenal milestones, we have become progressively oblivious of the bigger picture. Our astonishing strides in science and innovation, which were means to enhance our survival and prosperity, have become Frankensteins that threaten the very existence of our world.

Our pursuit of progress, largely defined by a linear vision of economic growth and consumption, has propelled us into an era where we are gradually but definitely devouring the planet. We pollute the air we breathe, the water we drink and the land that provides us sustenance. We have ushered in a new epoch, the 'Anthropocene', shaped by relentless human activity, based on exploitation rather than symbiosis.

As we map the stars and the mysteries of the cosmos beyond, we often overlook the spherical marvel beneath our feet and the intricate web of life that sustains it. The evolution that birthed us from the minutest of organisms now observes in silence as we teeter on the brink of self-destruction.

And yet, there is hope. For as long as we carry the flame of consciousness, there is the potential for change. A change in the way we live, the way we think, the way we relate to our environment and to each other. The question remains whether we, the pinnacle of evolution on Earth, can evolve past our self-imposed captivity. Will we choose to remember our humble beginnings, respect the intricate web of life upon which our survival depends, and chart a new path that harmonises our existence with the rhythms of nature.

For if we do not, the writhing amoeba in some distant primordial soup might one day look in puzzlement at the million-years-old ruins of a civilization that once had the power to shape its destiny, but chose instead to shape its doom. The choices we make today will determine the legacy we leave for the generations to come. We must not let our actions echo in eternity as a testament to our insensitivity and arrogance.

The cacophony was deafening, despair echoed through the void, an eternal symphony of torment and regret. It was the cries that rattled him the most—it wasn’t the burning flames or the inky darkness that caused discomfort, but the sounds. The never-ending wail of souls trapped in a torturous limbo, each shriek more desperate and ear-splitting than the last. He hated to admit it, but he even felt sympathy for them.

As the ruler of this realm, it pained him to hear their anguish. He knew each of their stories, each of their sins. He was a judge of darkness and evil, a punisher of the wicked. Yet, there was no satisfaction in his task, only a sense of duty and burden that weighed heavily upon him.

The souls were trapped here for reasons as varied as the sins that had damned them. From a brutally ambitious king who was lustful for conquest to a seemingly pious priest corrupted by greed, they all found their own circles in this Hell. Yes, each of them deserved their punishment, he had no doubts about that. Though, perhaps, there were very few who deserved such a wretched existence.

He pressed his gloved hand to the iron-wrought balcony that overlooked the tormented sea of souls. His heart ached with the calamity of the sight. His dark eyes flickered with an uncommon softness as he looked out at the damned souls. If he could feel pity, it would be for them. If he could shed tears, it would be for their irreversible fate. But he had given up those luxuries a long time ago. Compassion and mercy had no place in Hell, not even for its ruler.

There were times when he pondered upon the concept of redemption. Is it possible for a wicked soul to repent for its deeds? Is there a chance for the damned to earn their salvation? They were dangerous thoughts, disruptions in the status quo of his dominion. Dangerous, yet haunting. They stemmed from a shred of hope, a flicker of doubt, a question: what if Hell was not the end?

He dismissed these thoughts, hardening his heart against them. It was not his place to question the divine design. His purpose was to rule and to judge, not to redeem or to forgive. Yet, the screams, the cries of the broken continued to echo, their sorrow forever seared into every corner of this eternal inferno.

Conflicted and weary, he turned away from the despairing sight. For him, there was no respite, no solace. Wrapped in an endless cloak of darkness, he was the embodiment of hopeless eternity, of regret and damnation. He was destined to rule in the throes of this Hell, to exist amid the relentless wails of trillions of souls.

But still, there was a whisper within him, a quiet echo amongst the chaos, persistently pushing him towards an unthinkable idea. It was far-fetched, blasphemous even. Yet, the thought refused to fade, embedding itself into his heart and mind and echoing through every fiber of his being.

What if Hell could be something more than an instrument of eternal torment? What if Hell could be a place of redemption? The thought was tantalizing, fueling a spark of hope even in this undying darkness. 

For now, however, he could only listen to the terrified cries as they echoed forebodingly through his kingdom, a constant reminder of the eternal torment that was his realm.

Yes, Hell was bad enough, trillions of souls screaming out at once.

In a world that was once suffused with harmony and balance, light and dark coexisted, intertwined in an eternal ballet of cosmic proportions. Their unity symbolized the equilibrium of life and death, love and hatred, joy and sorrow. But, as the world matured and evolved, a shift occurred shaking the very foundation of this reality. 

Sixty years ago, an obscure force, ancient yet pristine, spawned an abyss driving a wedge between the light and dark, causing a catastrophic fallout. The separation of these two entities rent the very fabric of existence, casting a shocking reality that shook the world to its core.

The world was plunged into a state of discordant mayhem. The Light, known for its benevolence and life-giving properties, engulfed the world spreading hope, joy, warmth, but, without the balance offered by the Dark, it did not take long for the Light to become too immense and intense. Unchecked, it scorched whatever fell into its path, making the once thriving lands barren and parched.

Conversely, the realm where Dark reigned turned into an abyss of cold, quiet oblivion, devoid of life and warmth. Stripped of the Light's radiant energy, it became a desolate wasteland swirling in an eternal, horrifying vortex of despair and sorrow.

As the balance of the world continued to falter, prophecy of an ancient scripture echoed through time hinting towards salvation - a chosen one, born in the realm of chaos, carrying in their heart both light and dark. This individual, gifted with a unique ability to bridge both worlds, was the world’s only hope to mend the rift and restore harmony.

Years ticked by as the world waited with bated breath for the arrival of the prophesied one. Nothing happened for the longest time until mysteriously, one day, a child was born on the night the shadow of the eclipse covered the world. A spectacle of darkness and light in the sky heralded its birth. 

The child named Orion, exemplified everything the prophecy claimed. As he grew up, he showed signs of containing both the dark and the light within him, of being able to control them, and more importantly, to unite them. 

Now, as the world persists in its chaotic dance, the mystery remains whether Orion holds the power to achieve the astronomical feat of uniting light and dark? His journey ahead is fraught with trials and tribulations that will challenge his life, his mettle and his remarkable destiny. The hope of the world hangs in the balance as the prophecy is no guarantee of success, and the clock to salvation - or destruction - continues to tick down.

He couldn't withstand the love and affection shared between the two. Every stolen kiss, every loving glance, stung worse than the fiery pits of hell from where he emerged. He didn't want to admit it, not even to himself, but the green-eyed monster was rearing its ugly head. He was envious. 

No, not simply envious-he was in love. In love with Polly. How could he let this happen to himself? Demons were not designed to fall in love. They were creatures of chaos, turmoil, and darkness. Love was a human thing, a human weakness. But Polly was different.

She had the charm that none he'd come across possessed. Her bright blue eyes twinkling with innocence and mischief reminded him of the sparkling cerulean waters of the human realm corrupted with clear evil. Her graceful laughter reminded him of the melodious sounds echoing through endless tunnel-like caverns in his realm.

Seeing her with Kevin was enough to wreak havoc in his heart; it was a constant, torturous reminder that he'd never be able to hold her the same way. 'He's not even worth you, Polly,' he'd think. Kevin, a human with vanilla-flavored life incapable of understanding the depth of the tempest that was Polly. 

Her playful demeanor was a clear facade to the storm brewing inside her soul, a storm only Dave could weather. Like those tempestuous storms in his own realm, she too was a fatal combination of elegance, beauty, and risk.

His thoughts were interrupted as he saw Kevin lean in to kiss Polly. His grip on the boulder tightened—rough edges piercing his hell-hardened skin—purple-black with rage. The sight was repulsive, so he looked away. The heart, filled with agonizing pain and frustration, was seemingly shattering into fragments as his longing gaze fell on the oblivious Polly.

But Dave knew that this was his cross to bear, a punishment worse than any he could expect in hell. For falling in love with a human girl who they called Polly, and bearing the weight of a love unrequited, a tale as old as time, even for a demon.

Although Dave wasn't omnipotent, he carried an aura about him that seemed to affect everyone he interacted with. There was a magnetism to him, an irresistible pull that drew people in. His bright, piercing eyes had the ability to hold you in a gaze that felt like he was peering into the depths of your soul. And in many ways, he was.

Dave had a gift. A strange, eerie gift that he tried to keep under wraps. If he made eye contact with anyone for more than a few seconds, he could see their entire life, every memory, every secret, every joy and sorrow they had ever known. It was like flipping through a book, a comprehensive biography of sorts. But this was not an ability he had asked for or acquired, it was simply a part of him, as natural as his ability to breathe or think.

And it was not just the past that Dave could see. He was also able to glimpse into the future, but with less clarity. People's futures weren't as clear as written chapters, but rather as vague scribbles that could change or morph as decisions were made in the present. 

While some, in fear or awe, might perceive him as some sort of deity, Dave felt his curse limited his ability to form genuine connections. People would often find it discomforting when he knew more about them than they ever shared. Some called him a 'mind reader', others a 'psychic', some even thought him a 'witch'. 

However, Dave had learned to use his gift in ways that could benefit the world. He became an excellent mediator, able to resolve disputes by revealing what each party truly wanted and what their past had faced. As a counselor, he helped countless people by understanding their traumas and experiences in depth. And yet, he always bore his gift with a degree of melancholy.

Throughout his life, Dave had seen countless lives unfold before his eyes, had tasted the happiness, the heartbreak, the hope, and the despair of countless souls. Maintaining his own sanity in the face of all this turmoil was a challenge, but Dave had grown a great deal through his experiences and become somewhat of an emotional anchor. 

He had lived his life as an outsider, peeking into the worlds of others, supplementing the whispers of possibility with the hard truths of the past. And though he continued to walk his path with an air of dignity, deep down Dave yearned for the simplicity of just being Dave, rather than the all-knowing, all-seeing entity everyone perceived him to be.

Rogers continued to delve deep into the intricacies of my diagnosis. His office was a sophisticated room, full of certificates and plaques proclaiming his clinical acumen. Despite that, I couldn't shake off the gnawing uncertainty at the pit of my stomach.

"Jane, I understand that this is a huge blow to you. But it's not the end of the world. Insomnia is a complicated disorder, but with the right strategies and medical intervention, we can manage it effectively," he said, his face as steady as his voice.

I took a deep breath, trying to let the wave of relief wash over my initial shock. "What does this mean practically, Dr. Rogers?"

He leaned back, providing me the room to process this information. "Well, first things first. We are going to have to adjust your lifestyle a little: restricting stimulants like caffeine, maintaining regular sleep hours, and possibly introducing a short period of relaxation before you sleep. If these aren't sufficient, we will look at more intensive treatments like CBTI or medications."

I signed, my mind already racing with what these changes meant for my campus life, assignments, and social activities. "That means adjusting my whole schedule."

He nodded his acknowledgment. "Yes, initially, this might be challenging. But remember, Jane, this is not the last stop. This is the first step of getting better."

Even as my mind was swirling with fears and worries, somewhere in my heart, I knew I had to fight down this path. Leaving without seeing an end seemed terrifying, but so was living in this loop of sleeplessness, fatigue, and fear. I had a lot to figure out, a lot to change, but for the first time in a long while, I felt I had a sliver of control over my situation. And for now, that was enough.
