Sub-aquatic environments were harsh, and the citizens living in these colonies often faced health issues not seen on terrestrial planets. The pressure of the ocean, the constant hum and vibration from the colony structures, the lack of natural light - all these factors contributed to a host of psychological and physiological issues.

Neurotransplants, especially, were a boon when it came to combating these conditions. Enriched with AI assistance, these transplant systems served to maintain the mental health of the colonists, managing hormones, regulating sleep cycles, and ensuring optimal neural function.

Moreover, the implanted artificial neurons could adjust and compensate for the unusual underwater environment. These implants were often integrated with systems that controlled a host of other bodily functions, such as pressure resistance and oxygen absorption.

Augmentations, on the other hand, provided physical advancements that allowed humans to survive, thrive, and even excel in their subsurface homes. For instance, individuals often opted for secondary gill systems, allowing them to draw oxygen directly from the water in case of emergencies. Enhanced muscular and skeletal structures offered strength and resilience against water pressure.

Additionally, specialized augmentations allowed colonization and exploration of deeper, more alien parts of the ocean. Bioluminescent implants and ultraviolet vision capabilities came in handy when it came to braving the lightless depths. Other explorers opted for additional limbs or swimming aids, designed after the local aquatic fauna.

The use of neurotransplants and augmentations accelerated the development and growth of the ocean colonies. With these advancements, people could live healthier, longer lives, exploring the mesmerizing alien oceans they now called home.

With evolution and natural selection moving at their own steady pace, technology had provided an unmatched solution. Augmentations and neurotransplants effectively accelerated human adaptability, empowering colonies to comfortably inhabit planets that would otherwise be considered inhospitable. 

The immense symbolism of these innovations was not lost. In the vast, swirling ocean of stars and worlds, humanity had found a way to redefine its limits, riding the waves of scientific and technological progression, always pushing forward, deeper into the unknown.

I've been trying to think about this more recently; about the way time is running. Two weeks ago, marked the sixth year since Mom and Dad left us. Six years, they flew by so fast, and yet, they felt like eternity. But you know, Big Brother, I've realized it isn't about how long they've been gone, it's about what we've done with that time that matters.

In their absence, we've matured faster than most kids our age, we've learned to navigate life in a way we never expected to. You stepped into Dad's shoes; taking over his business and managing our finances while still continuing your studies. I watched, learned, and looked up to you, trying to fill the gap Mom left behind; cooking meals, doing laundry, taking care of our home, and you.

Their loss left a gaping hole in our hearts and lives but it isn't an abyss of sorrow. It became a source of motivation, pushing us to do better, to succeed, to make them proud. Mom and Dad might not be here physically, but they never truly left us. In each other, we see traces of them. I see Mom in your smile, your compassion, your unbending kindness. I see Dad in your determination, strength, resilience, the way you never back down no matter how tough things get.

Looking back, the initial fear and dread has transformed into an acceptance with a tinge of sadness. Yes, we miss them every day, but it's not just about the pain anymore. It's also about the priceless memories they've left us with, the values they instilled in us, and the lessons we've learned in their absence.

I remember how difficult it was in the beginning. The nights were the hardest. Sometimes, I would wake up in the middle of the night just to check if you were still there. Other nights I would dream about them, visualizing them with us. And on some nights, I used to sneak out just to look at the stars, imagining them looking over us in the form of those twinkling celestial bodies.

But we made it through, didn't we, Big Brother? We made it through with tenacity and courage that would have made Mom and Dad proud. Six years and it feels like we've lived a lifetime. We've experienced more in our young lives than many adults ever do.

The world may see us as two kids who lost their parents too soon. But I see us as a testament to human resilience, to strength in adversity, and above all, to the power of family. As we move forward, let's continue to live, not just for ourselves, but also for them, knowing they're with us every step of the way. In our victories, our losses, our struggles, and our triumphs, they’re there, smiling down on us.

I know we will face more challenges, but with you by my side, I believe we can face anything, Big Brother. So here's to you, to us, and to Mom and Dad. Here's to the future, to the love and light that they've left behind, and to the love and light we keep moving forward with. We've carried six years of their legacy, and we will keep carrying it, for a lifetime to come. After all, they live in us, through us, always.

You'd think that the rot and decay would be the worst of it, but in fact, it was another smell entirely that lingered at the forefront of my mind--a nauseating mix of burnt rubber, chemicals, and something metallic. A post-apocalyptic perfume that clung to your clothes and left a bitter taste in your mouth.

As we moved further into the compound, the repugnant odor became even more prevalent. It became clear that this was not only the scent of destruction but also death; the aftermath of a catastrophe that had left nothing but wreckage in its wake.

Even though we wore masks, the stench crept in, wrapping around our senses, and clinging for dear life. Despite our initial reticence to venture deeper, there really wasn't much of a choice at this point. We had to move forward; retreat wasn't an option.

Through the twisted metal, rubble, and detritus, we could faintly make out silhouettes of buildings that once stood proudly but now were gnarled remnants of a past reality. Everything else in sight was just an inky, formless maw of nothingness.

Hysterical laughter bubbled up from someone behind me, their sanity teetering on the edge of a precipice. It seemed macabre, but the laughter was a bitter release, a stark reminder of our humanity amidst chaos.

Fear clawed at the fringes of our group, threatening to consume us. But we moved doggedly on, driven by an urgency to find what was left of the world we once knew. 

Never before had I wished so much for the comforting scent of clean earth, or a fresh sea breeze, something to cleanse the palate of the fetid perfume of devastation that hung so potently in the air. But for now, all we had was the pungent smell of reality, a grim and undying reminder of the world that now was.

As I walked down the steps that led to the underground streets of the city, all the noise seemed to fade away. It was like stepping into another dimension; a dimension devoid of the city's chaos and incoherence. The clamor of the city was replaced by hushed whispers bouncing off the cold, stone walls. Suddenly, the vibrant and bustling city above felt lightyears away.

Down here, there was a sense of tranquility. An eerie silence filled the air and the towering buildings were replaced by narrow alleys with dimmed lights. Every footstep echoed on the pavement, bouncing off the walls, the sound echoing back, a somber song of solitude.

As I ventured deeper, I stumbled upon a beautifully lit boutique, warm light spilling out from its windows. Their bright reflection danced merrily on the cobblestone floor, a stark contrast to the surrounding monotone. It was tempting, a beacon of hope amongst the limbo, but I passed by, the need for solitude too strong to resist.

Walking further down the labyrinth-like underground, I found a small park, lush green amidst an ocean of stone, a breathing space. The moonlight streaming down from tiny windows above brought an enchanting glow to the place. Sitting on the solitary bench, bathed in the silvery glow of the moon, I took a quiet moment for reflection.

Maybe I took the decision too hastily. Maybe I shouldn’t have stepped down. Maybe I was running away from my problems instead of facing them. But that moment, under the cold light of moon, I realized that there was a peculiar peace in this solitude. A peace that calmed my anxieties, reassured my restless soul. I wasn't escaping from them, I was finding myself.

Exhaling a sigh of relief, I left the place with a newfound determination. I was ready to face the madness, the chaos, and the noise. My escape to the underground city had sharpened my perspective rather than dulling it. 

I don't know why I did it. I stepped down to get away from all of these people, to escape their madness. But in the end, this journey to solitude taught me more about my inner strength than any crowd ever could. The underground city of solitude served its purpose. Now it was time to step back up.

In our society, a world built upon the foundation of democratic principles, we advocate for the power and freedom of individual pursuits. Such freedom, we believe, should be afforded to everyone regardless of their socioeconomic status, gender, ethnicity, or age. We believe that each person is born with an innate potential, and it is the nurturing and cultivation of this potential that forms the basis of self-fulfillment. "Death by fulfillment", an ideology by which everyone is allowed to follow their dreams and ambitions until the end of their lives, ensures that each person exhausts their passion, skills, and efforts in a relentless pursuit of their own definition of success.

This concept of "death by fulfillment" differs greatly from a simple, one-dimensional definition of success. It is not just about achieving a certain status, wealth or societal recognition. In fact, it goes beyond an individual's achievement and looks into what they become in the process of reaching their life's zenith. Fulfillment, in this sense, implies a growth process that is self-directed, self-determined, and self-realizing, bringing the individual closer to a state of authentic happiness.

In essence, "death by fulfillment" asserts that everyone deserves the right and access to opportunities to explore, to learn, hone their skills, and execute their initiatives, so they may actualize the best version of themselves. Each person’s unique path to fulfillment not only contributes to their individual progression, but also propels societal advancement. When people are actively pursuing their dreams, they are more motivated and committed, learn from mistakes and keep improving, resulting in a productive, innovative, and forward-moving society.

However, to create a society where "death by fulfillment" can thrive requires a few key conditions. We need an equitable education system that nurtures curiosity and provides the knowledge and resources necessary for individuals to discover their passions and pursue their ambitions without barriers. We need a professional sphere that values diverse pathways to success and offers a range of fulfilling career choices.

Moreover, the pursuit of "death by fulfillment" should also encourage balance and mental well-being. This means providing support systems that promote resilience, equipping individuals with coping mechanisms for dealing with stress and failure, and identifying measures of success that value fulfillment and happiness as much as productivity and societal contribution.

In such a society, "death by fulfillment" transcends to becoming not just an individualistic aim, but a collective ethos. When everyone is offered equal opportunities to pursue their passions and realize their dreams, we create a society that is abundant in fulfillment, where individuals thrive, and thereby, communities flourish. This is the heart of "Death by fulfillment." The pursuit of not just dreams, but of lives well-lived, of individual happiness and societal progress.

I duck, barely avoiding the detriment of shattering porcelain, but the contents still splatter across my attire. My once pristine suit absorbs the cool liquid, spots of tea darkening against the light fabric. 

"As many times as I inform her of the physically impossible task of maintaining the same pot temperature in this huge mansion, she never seems to grasp it," I lament internally. I breathe deeply to reign in the impulses of my less professional self, pushing away the sharp retort that tickles the back of my tongue.

"Yes, ma'am," I reply with imposed politeness, loosening my marred tie and unbuttoning the drenched jacket. "I'll make you a fresh pot immediately."

She has already stalked off by the time I finish speaking, her heels clicking an infuriating rhythm against the marble flooring as she retreats to her private library on the upper floors. 

The echo of her disapproval looms heavily on the silent halls, leaving me with just the dripping sound of tea. I shake my head slightly, dabbing at my suit with a handkerchief, mindful of the remnants of my job.

'Just until I find something better', I keep reminding myself as my shoes squeak on the wet floor, making way towards the kitchen.

In the face of Mistress McGregor’s boundless wrath, I could only maintain a poker face, reminding myself that this household helped to secure my survival in the expensive city that is New York.

The kitchen is my sanctuary amidst the chaos — a realm shielded by wafts of baked goods and various exotic teas. Here, I am my own master, contradicting my otherwise subservient stance.

With an exaggerated roll of my eyes to an audience of knives and stirring spoons, I begin the tedious task of brewing a fresh pot of tea which, much like my suit, will definitely not be appreciated.

I was all the way across town at my flat and my suit was still hanging, unworn at the venue. Rush hour in the city was notoriously bad, and although I knew the shortest way by heart, chances were pretty high I'd get caught in a bottleneck somewhere in the middle and that would inevitably delay my arrival.

Every second counted. I grabbed my phone, wallet, and keys, too distracted to notice I left my tying knot guide behind, my tie hanging around my neck like a schoolboy's. I jumped in my car, switched on the ignition and zipped out my apartment, breaking carefully calculated speed limits and praying to all the gods I knew that the traffic officers had somehow taken today off.

The thrill of urgency pumped adrenaline into my veins, focus sharpening my senses like a cat's strutting on thin fences under the moonlight. I didn't even wait for the lights, making bold swerves, negotiating tight turns, and just barely missing pedestrian crossings. To say I was defying death itself wasn't an exaggeration. On any normal day, I would never even dream of driving like this. But then again, today was no normal day.

I could already envision my suit, perfectly pressed with its polished buttons gleaming under the soft, warm bulb inside the dressing room. And me, all dishevelled and sweaty, the complete antithesis of how a groom was supposed to look on his big day. Oh yes, I was the groom. And I was late for my own wedding.

I could practically hear my best man Dave, his voice looping in my head smothered in amused sarcasm, "That's Rich for you, always the dramatic one."

Yeah, this was definitely one for the books. One glance at my wrist watch and a trickle of sweat made its path down my forehead, crawling down my cheek in slow motion. 30 minutes to go and still 15 miles to cover. The cityscape blurred past me as I sped on praying for a miracle.  

I glanced at the rear-view mirror and smirked mildly, my reflection mirrored my predicament; tie untied, shirt half buttoned, hair all mussed-up like some character from a dystopian series. It wasn't exactly an image of a composed, ready-to-marry groom.  

But if there is one thing I have learned from the chaos of city life, it's that we have no control over time or traffic, but we can always control our response to it. And so, I drove on, hoping for the best while holding onto the determined spirit of love that had led me this far.

Boy mourns loss of girl. He spends his days and nights thinking about what went wrong, wallowing in self-pity and regret. He sees her face in every crowd, hears her laughter in every song. The world has lost its color and his life feels emptier and colder than before. He misses her more than he could have imagined.

Months pass, gradually he learns to cope with the pain. He starts engaging in activities that once gave him joy; reading, painting, cooking. The smell of his favorite dish once again brings a smile to his face and not a pit in his stomach. He embraces these moments of happiness, however fleeting, knowing it's a small but significant step towards healing.

In the process, he discovers a new passion; poetry. He pours his heart and feelings into words. His pain, his loss, his love, and his longing. The words flow from him like a river, offering him a cathartic release. He doesn't share these poems with anyone, they're for him, part of his personal journey of healing.

One day while attending a small local poetry event, he musters the courage to share a piece with the audience. His voice trembles as he reads his deeply personal words. He expected awkward silence but to his surprise, his poem was greeted with a rousing applause.

Among the crowd, a girl is left particularly moved by his words. She has never heard poetry so raw, so beautiful, so powerful. She feels an instant connection, like his words spoke to her soul. Intrigued, she approaches him after the event.

0They start talking, and he is captivated by her passion for art, her sparkling green eyes, her radiant smile. She, on the other hand, is bowled over by his honesty, his depth, and his resilience. They talk and talk, forgetting about time, forgetting about the world around them.

It's not instant love, but a slow build up; a bud blooming gradually into a beautiful flower. Boy meets another girl. This time, boy doesn't lose girl.

Instead, they grow together, supporting and standing by each other through life's ups and downs. They share dreams, fears, joys, and sorrows. And most importantly, they share love; a love that is deep, pure, and resilient. A love that heals old wounds and gives life a new meaning.

Boy loses girl, boy finds himself, boy finds love again. This is not just a love story, it's a story of self-discovery, healing, and second chances. And sometimes, that's all one needs in life.

Dave rented a modest beachfront property in Nassau. Completely encircled by coconut trees, the house offered a panoramic view of the vast turquoise ocean. The golden beach, glittering under the sun, stood in stark contrast to the cityscape he was used to seeing. It was pure paradise.

Yet, paradoxically, there are certain moments in every individual’s life when they might contemplate the possible effects of their non-existence. This feeling is not too dissimilar from the one experienced by George Bailey, the protagonist of 'It's a Wonderful Life'. 

It is in such moments too, that we must remember the invaluable lesson this film teaches us - every life, no matter how seemingly insignificant, touches many others and makes an impact often unbeknown to the individual. However, unlike George, we do not possess the power to envision the consequences of our non-existence. We cannot see the butterfly effect we'd have set into motion, the lives we'd have impacted, the difference we'd have made – and that’s okay. Because the worth of our lives should not be determined by the number of people we’ve directly influenced, but rather by the sincerity, love, and kindness with which we’ve lived.

The yearning to be erased from the annals of time often stems from feelings of pain, loneliness, inadequacy, and failure. But as 'It's A Wonderful Life' poignantly illustrates, the real strength lies in confronting these feelings, recognizing our impact, and understanding our worth. After all, every individual is woven irrevocably into the fabric of time, their existence knotting and intertwining with the existence of others, creating a tapestry that is both beautiful and irreplaceable.

No one, therefore, should choose to erase their existence from the records of time because, without them, the world wouldn't have been quite the same.

My name is Ben Warren, a simple man with one grand passion - exploration. I was always fascinated by the unknown and intrigued by the idea of discovering uncharted lands. So, in the summer of 1972, I seized my chance to embark on an adventure that changed my life forever. At the age of 20, I bade goodbye to my family in our small township of Hampshire and set out to explore those parts of the world I had only read about in books.

All I can say is that each day brought its own kind of excitement, its own thrill, and its own strange contentment. I traveled, I learned, I adapted. From the Orient to the Occident, the Arctic to the Antarctic, deserts to rainforests, ancient civilizations to ultramodern cities, I saw, soaked in, and survived it all.

In those 45 years of solitude and exploration, there have been countless times when I have confronted dangers that could've been my end. But I believe that in every such instance, I found a new beginning. With time, the cycle of nature's fury and majesty became the rhythm of my life. It was challenging, and often it was daunting, but never did I regret the path I chose.

Yet, despite my love for the unknown, in the silence of the night or in those few quiet moments after an intense day, I found my thoughts drifting back to what I had left behind. To my mom's laughter echoed around our cozy house and my dad's tales of his youthful adventures. To my childhood friend, Jenny, who filled my adolescence with carefree joy. As time passed, I often wondered, did I trade one adventure for another? Could those simple pleasures compare to this vast world of experiences?

Perhaps, there was a part of me that never left home. Maybe it rested in the letters I posted to them from every nook and corner of the world I visited. In my heart, despite being thousands of miles away, I never felt completely detached or forlorn. The memories acted as a beacon that kept the connection alive, even amidst great separations and silences.

As I look back on these 45 years, I realize that exploration isn't just about discovering new landscapes, but about understanding oneself. Living away from everyone familiar, I discovered dimensions of myself that I wasn’t aware of. I discovered resilience, courage, patience, and most importantly, the universal language of empathy and humanity.

Tomorrow, as I turn 65, I plan to embark on an expedition of a different kind. A journey back to my roots, my home, to my long-cherished people and memories. I am excited, scared, and filled with bittersweet emotions.

I find myself wondering, after 45 long years, will it still feel like home? Will they still remember me? Unanswered questions flood my mind, creating a unique anticipation. There is a thrill I had almost forgotten — a thrill not of venturing into the unknown, but of returning to the known after so long. What will await me there? I don't know, but I'm ready to find out. Because every great journey, after all, is about coming back home.

The man speaking, an old, gnarly figure of a man named Joe, had skin like worn leather that had seen too much sun, too much wind, and too much age. He sat behind the bar of a low-rent dive - the kind where people went to drown their sorrows, not to celebrate.

Despite this, I loved Sherman. His coffee-brown eyes, his silky fur which bore the color of the setting sun, and his relatively large size, owing to his German Shepherd ancestry, was what initially attracted me to him.

Sherman was not what you would call a 'typical' dog. He wouldn't wag his tail at the sight of me, or jump up and down in joy, or shower me with slobbery kisses. Instead, he maintained a dignified distance, a stance filled with aloof grace that left most friend and family dazzled. 

Taking him for walks was like being on a treadmill. His pace was slow, deliberate, not like other dogs who liked to dart here and there, yanking their owners off their feet. Sherman was... different. He wasn't a dog one could 'command'. He was, in many ways, like an old soul trapped in a dog’s body, calm, composed, forever thoughtful.

But it wasn't always this way. As a puppy, Sherman was just like any other. Hyperactive, always seeking attention, gnawing at furniture. But as years passed on, something changed...

Rather than running after tossed frisbees or tennis balls, Sherman would lie under the shade of a tree, peacefully observing the world with patient eyes. His placid demeanour was something one couldn't ignore; it often felt like he was an old man, wise beyond his years or, in his case, dog years.

Despite his lack of traditional dog-like characteristics, Sherman commanded a gravitas that made me proud to be his owner. His uniqueness and his ability to break the dog stereotype made people remember him.

People often remarked on his lack of 'obvious' affection. But ultimately, it was the silent companionship, the peaceful coexistence in each other's company that mattered the most to us. It took me a while to understand this - the fact that love does not always have to be expressed through licks, wags, and fetching balls. 

Sherman showed me that silent companionship can be just as meaningful as loud expressions of love. He didn't need to 'fetch' to show his fondness. His simple presence by my side, his aloof-yet-loyal gaze was more than enough to communicate his intricate emotions - the same way not everyone needs to shout from rooftops to genuinely express their love.

Despite all the quirkiness, Sherman was my buddy, my old, composed, dignified buddy. His silence spoke volumes, his eyes told stories, he was so much more than just a 'good boy'. He was, in short, an enigma wrapped in a canine.

We were twenty of us, bestowed upon this "gift" by a crazed alchemist, who claimed it to be the next step in the development of humanity. Elixir of Life, he had named it. No more aging, no more dying; we would be as immortal as the gods of yore. The allure was too strong to resist, and we drunketh from the fount of unending youth.

But, only after the passage of several decades did we realize the dark underbelly of this "God’s blessing," as the alchemist had called it. Yes, our bodies ceased to age, our wrinkles smoothened, and our hair retained its youthful color. But what of our hearts and our minds, that frayed and wore under the weight of centuries?

We became spectators of the play of life, seeing our loved ones wither away, while we stayed static. Our children, spouses, friends; we saw them all shrivel and rot as we stood by, helplessly. Our hearts wept while our bodies laughed, mocking at the inevitable death. What's immortality but a sham when everything around us is mortal?

With each passing century, the world changed, society evolved, but we remained suspended in a time that didn't exist anymore. We became relics, artifacts of a time long since passed, struggling to fit into the jigsaw of the now. Every new dawn brought with it a fresh wave of melancholy, for we knew we were doomed to witness a thousand more; alone, lost, and bereft.

Aging, as it turns out, is not the curse. Everything in nature grows old and perishes, paving the way for the new. Living is growing, changing, evolving, and then finally passing on. It's not a chain, but rather, a river, flowing unencumbered towards its ultimate destination – the ocean of oblivion. It's the cycle of life, beautiful and unavoidable.

In seeking to escape death, we lost out on life. Imprisoned within our own unchanging skin, we yearned for the liberation that aging brought, the peace of closure, of knowing that we had lived a life full of changes and that it was time now to rest.

So beware of such mirages as immortality. They're not a blessing, but a chimera that chains you to eternal solitude and unhappiness. Seek not to eliminate aging, but to embrace it, for it is the only true companion in our journey through existence. Aging and, eventually, death; these are not the enemy, but the natural conclusion to the story of life.

My heart was pounding as I watched the lights flicker and die out one by one; the storm was swallowing the city. The wind was howling like a pack of wolves, tearing at my clothes and whipping my hair into a frenzy. I gritted my teeth, willing my body to endure the cold, the rain, the storm that was acting as the perfect metaphor for my inner turmoil.

My thoughts were with the inhabitants locked within the towering stone walls. The people who had lived their lives sheltering themselves, isolating themselves from the world. Simple, oblivious folks who had no knowledge about the turmoil brewing on the outside.

I turned my gaze upwards. Heavy, menacing clouds roiled overhead, their darkness broken only by the jagged streaks of lightning that spider-webbed across the sky. The thunder that followed was like a percussion instrument in Mother Nature’s orchestra, deafeningly loud and staggeringly relentless.

I took a step back, retreating from the edge of the hill. Cool, wet earth squelched beneath my boots, the grassroots struggling to cling onto them. I cast another glance at Canning, its outline blurred behind veils of rain.

I felt a pang in my heart, a pang of guilt for leaving them, a pang of concern for their ignorance. But there was something deeper, something unsettling. It was fear, fear for what awaited me.

I was about to embark on a journey, a journey that I had postponed for far too long. I had a mission to accomplish, a score to settle. An ancient arcana had chosen me; I was supposed to ride the storm, to whisper the secrets, to change the inevitable, and to stop the forthcoming doom.

Taking a deep breath, I accepted the wetness, the cold, the chaos. I accepted my destiny and the responsibilities that laid heavy on my shoulders. Fear left me, replaced with determination, courage, and purpose.

As the final lights of Canning vanished, swallowed by the storm, I turned away from the city. I slid one foot in front of the other, moving further into the howling wind with a resolution in my heart. The journey had begun.

Canning would have to face its storm alone, as I faced mine.

"Zorak! Zorak, for the love of all things intergalactic, will you kindly grace me with your attention?" I bellowed towards the murky depths of my backyard.

A particularly strong gust of wind pulled the screen door from my grip, and it swooshed shut with a loud, tingling bang. I grumbled, bracing myself against the alien biting cold that seemed to leach from Zorak’s makeshift habitat to the rest of the yard.

Finally, a figure of impenetrable darkness began to detach itself from the surrounding murk. The alien features of Zorak became discernible under the faint, bluish glow of the backyard lights. Bathed in this unnatural illumination, his fluorescent eyes radiated an almost ethereal, hypnotic beauty.

"Earthling," he intoned, in a voice that resembled a foghorn more than anything, "what's the matter?"

I sighed deeply. "Zorak, is there any particular reason why you've decided to turn the swimming pool into a ‘Trans-Dimension Portal Repair Facility'?"

"I had to, Earthling. Or do you want to deal with an average Tuesday evening morphing into a prehistoric era due to temporal leakage?"

Despite my annoyance, a tiny smile tugged at the corner of my lips. Neither of us had any idea what an 'average Tuesday evening' was anymore. Ever since Zorak crash-landed in my backyard and took residence, every day had been anything but normal.

I asked him, "And the refrigerator? You've also turned that into a... what was it... 'Quantum Cooler'?"

He offered an apologetic shrug with his hulking shoulders - a gesture I had taught him.

"I assure you, Earthling, it was a necessity. In my defense, I reiterated the importance of stable cold storage for extra-dimensional engine components."

Dialed down into the details of our curt living arrangement, I realized Zorak was just trying to get home. And, as much as we argued, underneath all the alien humor and an unlikely friendship, I understood that I was his only chance to go back.

"Alright, Zorak," I said, "Here's the thing, Steel grocery or wooden cart home? For you, it might look mundane, but for us earthlings, it's essential. If you're going to be here and use my stuff, there are rules, okay?"

Zorak blinked his phosphorescent eyes, nodded. Maybe he didn't understand. Maybe he did. But one thing is for sure - tomorrow won't be an average Wednesday.

His once vibrant and commanding eyes remained hazy, clouded with worry and despair. The intricate crown, which had always sat proudly upon his head, now felt heavy, perpetually reminding him of the burden of kingship. The tapestry detailing the history of triumph and prosperity seemed to be mocking him.

He glanced around the mighty throne room, adorned with the golden-encrusted armor of his ancestors, their polished shields reflecting his dejected countenance. The banners, emblazoned with the royal crest of a fierce silver wolf biting a sword, hung limply as though it too had suffered his loss.

His kingdom, the once prosperous Norland, was under siege. The enemy forces had managed to overcome their defenses, forcing the proud king's men into a hasty retreat. His failure to protect his people filled him with a deep sense of shame as he thought of the impending doom approaching his lands.

His once reliable advisors who always had answers now sat somber, quietly reflecting on the critical situation. Despite their wisdom and experience, they were bereft of a solution, their faces ashen with dread. This great crisis had snuffed out the blazing fire that once symbolized their indomitable spirit.

Suddenly, the monstrous doors of his throne room creaked open. His eldest son, a brave and courageous prince adorned in blood-splattered armor, stepped inside. His face was cut and bruised, but his eyes were set in a fierce determination that cut through the gloom of despair surrounding his father. 

The King shifted in his throne, his melancholy gaze softening as he looked upon his heir. The Prince strode forward, his voice echoing against the stone walls. 

"We have been pushed back, Father. Beaten. But we have not lost. We will not surrender."

The King’s heart stirred with a flicker of newfound hope. His son was right. They were the proud people of Norland, the descendants of warriors and conquerors. They had faced defeat, yes, but they would rise again. They had always risen… and they would continue to do so.

His back straightened, his tired eyes hardened into a renewed determination matching that of his son's. As he stood, the crown didn't feel as heavy anymore. In the midst of their darkest hour, there was still hope. They would fight back. They would reclaim their land and protect their people. They would not crumble. They would survive. For they were Norlanders.

“Return to the battlefield, my son,” the King instructed, his voice echoing strength and resolve, "We will turn the tide. We. Will. Not. Lose."

And thus, amidst the trials of a brutal siege, The Great King's spirit rekindled, illuminating the halls of the fortress brighter than any victory tale inscribed in the royal tapestry. The imminent victory would be fraught with sacrifice, but he knew it would go down as the greatest tale of resilience, courage, and ultimate victory in the history of Norland.

The news of Fortuna's message aroused a mix of emotions among the people. Some saw it as a divine prophecy; others, considering it a hoax. As scientists worked on making sense of Fortuna's words, the earth's conditions gradually stabilized, and people started adapting to the new normal.

In the years that followed, the presence of Fortuna transformed the human outlook toward the cosmos. People now gazed at the sky, not with trepidation, but with a profound sense of awe and curiosity. They were reminded every day of the mystery and wonder that lay beyond the earthly realm.

The realization that humankind was not alone in the cosmos prompted a new era of discovery and exploration. The space agencies and private enterprises all over the world redirected their energies towards unpicking the secrets of Fortuna.

As humanity began to decipher the mysterious entity, unknown technologies were discovered, extinct diseases cured and age-old philosophies debunked. While Fortuna's presence was initially threatening, humanity adapted and progressed.

Years into Fortuna's appearance, humankind was no longer in a state of panic. Instead, awe and appreciation took over. Fortuna, the celestial entity that once seemed a precursor of doom, had instead ushered in a new era of enlightenment and progression.

It was indeed the dawn of a new age - the age of Fortuna. The entity that took up a third of the sky had become a symbol of the vast unknown and the limitless possibilities that existed beyond the familiar constellations in the heavens above. Despite its intimidating size and initial chaos, Fortuna proved to be a catalyst for human evolution. It inadvertently guided humanity toward a new understanding of life, the universe, and everything in between.

Opening the door, I came face to face with a figure from my past I had long forgotten. The man before me hadn't aged a day since the last time I saw him. 

"Sergeant Moro?" I asked incredulously, my eyes flicking over his familiar craggy features and the faint hint of pine that still clung to his old military jacket.

"Indeed, it's me," he replied in his low, grizzled voice I instantly remembered from twenty years ago. "Are you going to invite me in or am I meant to conduct our business standing in your doorway?"

I moved aside, a thousand questions whirling through my mind. Moro was my commanding officer back when I’d served in the army, was tough as nails and had a reputation for popping up where he was least expected. But what was he doing here? I hadn't heard from him since I'd left the military, preferring a quieter civilian life.

"Moro, not to be rude, but what are you doing here?" I asked as politely as I could while I shut the door behind him.

He looked around my small apartment, a hint of sadness crossing his weathered features before finally meeting my gaze. In his hand, he held out a small, sealed envelope. The insignia of our old unit was pressed into the wax seal. 

"I'm on a...personal mission," he began, his eyes shifting away as though haunted by some unseen ghosts. "I need your help."

I took the envelope from him, warming it in my hands. The cotton bond paper was smooth, expensive, and the seal shone under my living room lights. A sense of military nostalgia swept over me—a pang of yearning for the structured feel that only military life could bring.

Resting the envelope on the side table, I gestured towards the vacant seat. "Have a seat, Sergeant. Looks like we need to catch up."

And so we did. I didn't know what I was expecting when I heard the knock. Certainly not a man from my past and even more so, a call from a past life I left behind. But as the night progressed, I found myself considering a return to the world I had left behind, bearing the responsibilities of a forgotten sergeant and a sealed envelope.

Fractured neon digits pierced the darkness - 5:30 A.M. Sleep clawed desperately as the shrill beep struggled to snatch him away. Blinking, he reached out to silence the alarm, his fingers brushing the cold surface of the nightstand before colliding with the unforgiving solidity of the clock. 

The room was filled with silence again, a silent echo that hummed in his ears as he laid back down and stared up into the darkness. Distant memories of warmth and sleep beckoned, but they were fleeting, fading with every passing second. He was a creature of habit, and despite the allure of slipping back into his dreams, he was doomed to obey the norms established by his routine.

Rubbing the sleep out of his eyes, he threw back the warm cocoon of blankets and exposing himself to the icy chill that swept the room. The warmth of his bed was quickly replaced by the cruel sting of cold from the wooden flooring beneath him. The old, creaky floor groaned with each step as he made his way towards the bathroom.

In the harsh bathroom light, his reflection greeted him. Bags under his eyes, a day-old stubble, and the slightly slouched posture of a man carrying the weight of the world on his shoulders. With a splash of cold water on his face, he embraced the jolt of energy the shock offered.

Silently he moved around the room preparing for the day. Clothes scattered around, hastily picked up in an effort to create some semblance of order before he faced the world outside. The cold, unfeeling darkness of the room shared a chilling resemblance with his life off-late. A gloomy existence devoid of cheer, but routine nonetheless. 

Despite the trappings of his world, the alarming precision of his routine was a comfort. The mundane repetitiveness, so dull, yet reassuring. After all, breaking free from the fearful dark, embracing the colder morning, and tackling the relentless grind of the day was his practiced ritual. 5:30 A.M. was the start of yet another day in his life, a day that promised of things to come, lurking around the shadowy bends of time, waiting to unfold.

He blinked, trying to adjust to the enveloping darkness, but it made no difference. He was alone, in some unknown place, blanketed in an unnerving absence of light.

Lifting his hand, he frowned, realizing he could barely see the faint outline. The unsettling clunk sound echoed through the vast emptiness again, severing the silence. It wasn't just the sound that startled Sabir, it was also the unfamiliar cold sensation he felt on his palm when trying to identify the source of that noise.

He rolled his hand over, feeling something solid, cold, and somewhat rough. Steel, perhaps? The clunking sound continued to punctuate the blackness at steady intervals, akin to a heartbeat. Was it machinery? A clock? Sabir wasn’t sure.

Attempting to quell the rising panic, he reminded himself to take deep, measured breaths; in and out, in and out. His heart pounded, echoing in the percussive symphony of the clunk, clunk, clunk.

Sabir rose to his feet tentatively, still holding onto the cold, rugged, metal object. The darkness was relentless. Without sight, Sabir had to navigate relying on his other senses. His fingertips explored the object tracing its contours and edges, trying to estimate its dimensions. It felt large and was undoubtedly fastened to the ground. The source of the mechanical clunking noise was this very object.

Inching away from the object, he tried to explore the surrounding space. His feet tapped hesitantly over the cold cement floor, his fingertips just brushing the damp stone walls. Sabir sensed more than saw the confined space he was in. Was it a cell of some kind? A question that opened up a whole new level of dread.

The darkness weighed heavily on him; it felt almost physical, pressing down on his shoulders and wrapping around him like a shroud. The sound persisted. Clunk. Clunk. Clunk. It was too rhythmic to be random, too purposeful.

Sabir steeled himself and decided to do what he could within his power. If he was in a prison, or somewhere similar, eventually someone or something would come. Before that happened, he needed information. And for information, he would have to explore—no matter how frightening the prospect was.

Engulfed in darkness and guided by fear, Sabir steeled his nerves and stepped forward. The clunking sound was his unwelcome companion, sounding like the sinister ticking of a threat yet to unfold. His journey into the unseen had just begun.

But what kept his heart pounding at a steady, thrilling rate was ghost hunting.

That night, like many nights before, Gage found himself on the dark roads, the neon glow of city lights long gone behind him. The destination was an old, abandoned mansion nestled deep in the mountains. Half-eaten by nature, the mansion stood tall and eerie under the starless sky. Ivy crawled up its once pristine walls, windows stared hollow and the massive, gnarled tree beside seemed to swirl in whispers of the wind, playing endless symphony to the rampant rumors of the mansion being haunted. 

Gage stepped out of his car, his boots crunching the gravel as he took out his ghost hunting kit from the trunk. It consisted of: a camcorder, a digital voice recorder, EMF meter, thermal imaging camera, and a flashlight. No amateur tools like Ouija boards or divining rods for him; Gage was a professional ghost hunter. 

He paused to soak in the energy around him. Frosty gusts of wind swept hair off his face and every muscle in his body tingled with anticipation. There was nothing like the thrill of stepping into an unknown place, chasing the shadows and tracking down the cold spots. It was hunting, not for deer or rabbits, but for answers. Answers to questions most people were too afraid to ask. 

Pulling his jacket tighter, Gage started towards the massive front doors, but not before taking one last glance back into the night where his car rested. This was his point of no return, his last chance to back out and retreat into safety. However, Gage was not the kind to back down. No, he was the one who chased the whispers in the dark, found solace in the eerie silence of the haunted, hitched his pulse on the thrill of the unseen.

A wide, daring grin cut through his typically stern features as he pushed through the creaky doors into the heart of the mansion. Darkness waited inside, but it was a welcoming darkness, the kind that hides mysteries and tales, the kind that beckoned the brave and foolish. And armed with his kit, guided by his curiosity and courage, Gage stepped into the unknown, ready to conquer the fears that lay hidden in the veil of the night.

After all, one does not become a ghost hunter if he runs scared of the dark. You become one when you realize that the thrill of the hunt, the swoop in the stomach, and the rush of adrenaline when you encounter the unknown are some of the most intoxicating sensations in the world. They were to Gage, at least.

The excitement in the air was palpable as friends greeted each other after the long summer break. Laughter and chatter filled the air, the fleeting moment of peace before the arrival of our homeroom teacher. I twirled my pencil in my fingers, looking around at the familiar faces. The classroom had a mild scent of fresh paint, a telltale sign of renovation over the summer.

I was positioned at an ideal spot - right in the center, neither too close nor too far from the chalkboard. Just because I was a wallflower didn't mean I didn't take my grades seriously. This year was important; I had my eye set on a scholarship and was ready to work my butt off.

Friendships had shifted over the summer, like tectonic plates, they moved slowly but surely forming new alliances and creating new rifts. Even from my vantage point, I could see the subtleties of this social restructuring - the shy glances, the knowing looks. I watched it all with an amused detachment, the uninvolved observer, a silent spectator.

The classroom door creaked open then, cutting through the rhythmic chatter. A collective silence swept across the room as Mr. Anderson, our homeroom teacher, walked in. He was a stocky man with a bald pate, glasses perched precariously on the ridge of his nose.

"Good morning, students," he greeted, placing his briefcase on the table with a soft thud. His eyes scanned the room, a faint smile playing on his lips. 

"Welcome to junior year, class," he said, the smile widening. "I hope you're all as excited for this year as I am."

I nodded along with the rest of the students, a sense of anticipation swirling in my stomach. Little did I know then, it would indeed turn out to be an unforgettable year – a year of life lessons, heartbreaks, triumphs, and discoveries. And all of it would start here, from this center spot in my homeroom class.

"Ding- another day without incident, gentlemen. I am proud of you," chimed the tannoy again, its synthetic voice inflected with an edge of cheerful warmth that was quite unsettling coming from a machine.

Craig let out a hearty, genuine laugh, his teeth flashing white against his grizzled beard. "I swear Axel, this robot sounds more human every day."

"I think it's programmed to adapt in response to our human tendencies." Axel replied, wiping his forehead with his oil-streaked bandana. He let his gaze settle on the identifier plate screwed into the tannoy's mechanical neck - model A.I. P156. The upper echelon of robotic technology; fully autonomous, artificial intelligence capable of learning and adapting, much like a human child. 

Still smiling, Craig waved off Axel's technobabble. "All I'm saying is, it would be nice if the rest of us could learn to do our jobs without any accidents for almost two millennia."

Both men laughed then, fatigue forgotten for a moment as they reveled in the lightness of their camaraderie amidst the grinding monotony of the mechanical behemoth they worked in.

"Ding. Thank you, Craig. I am trying my best." The rote pronouncement of the A.I. was at such a perfect lull in the conversation that both men paused, glancing at each other in surprise.

They didn't have long to ponder the unsettling accuracy of the machine's timing; the grating alarm of the forklift rose above the cacophony of the assembly line, signaling more crates requiring their attention.

"Alright, back to the grindstone," Axel said, tightening his grip on the control handles. "Remember, we can't let P156 steal all the glory now, can we?"

The P156 continued its routine, firm and unwavering, as the men got back to their tasks. While its performance was flawless, it wasn’t aware of the pride or satisfaction of a job well done or even the harsh realities of manual labor that these humans had to endure. It merely calculated, executed, and learned - with no comprehension of the men's sweat, camaraderie, or even their half-serious rivalry.

And thus, the day rolled on, marked not just by the pulsating hum of machinery and man's labor, but also by the robotic chime, a testament to another day gone, another day without an accident, and the casual banter between machinery and men.

TITLE: In the Claws of the Viper

Following in the footsteps of his mentor, Robert "Viper" Carter continued his late-night excursions, hunting down and battling members of the Black Thorn. Things, as they say, were about to get personal.

One evening, as the biting wind of winter sang through the dark streets, Viper received a message. It was an anonymous tip about a Black Thorn gathering in the south of the city. The source of the tip was questionable, yet he had grown desperate, and decided to take the leap.

With his sleek black suit, guns in holster, and eyes that could burn through solid ice, Viper made his way south. He had travelled through these streets countless times, knowing every alleyway, each crack in the pavement. The city was a living, breathing beast, and Viper, the blood coursing through its veins.

Reaching the isolated building the tip-off had mentioned, Viper slipped effortlessly into the shadows. Just as he was about to make his move, he felt a presence behind him—a menacing entity, a predator waiting for the right moment to strike.

Turning, he met the cool gaze of the one person he least expected: Vanessa – a former lover turned Black Thorn associate.

Her appearance was unexpected, adding another layer to the complex puzzle. Vanessa held secrets he needed to unravel to destroy the Black Thorn. And he knew he had to tread carefully, for Vanessa, his estranged love, may very well end up being the key to this entire mission. A battle for truth and survival had just begun. Little could Viper know then, it was going to be a perilous path stepping out of the shadow of John Wick's legacy.

As the snow began to fall, Viper glanced once more at the building ahead, steeling himself for what lay within. And so, he stepped into the abyss, armed not only with his weapons but a resolve to extract the truth and save the city he called home.

I steadily prepped my station, making absolutely sure that everything was in its proper place and visually pleasing. I was his boss and, implicitly, the one who had to enact his potential removal. Alex had been with us for six months, and while he'd shown glimpses of promising talent, his consistency had been found wanting. His tenuous position in the company was made worse by an incident last week when he had lost his temper and embarrassed not just himself, but also the company in front of our client.

His wayward behaviour had led to a few complications - but it was his creative brilliance that had seen him recruited in the first place. He was a veritable gem that needed polishing, but after much deliberation among the board members, I had been given the arduous task of deciding his fate in the company.

As the day progressed, I watched him with caution, trying to register every detail of his work. That day, he showed up on time and got straight to work, not wasting a moment. I could see the apprehension he carried, given by his occasional glances towards me. His work was detail-oriented and methodical, surprising me and the rest of our team given his usual hasty and impulsive nature. 

By lunchtime, my opinion was starting to soften. All his flaws seemed magnified by my scrutiny, yet, offset by his attention to detail. An intense internal struggle unfolded as I wrestled with my decision. I was not just weighing the fate of an individual, but potentially the future of the company.

It was nearing the end of the day when Alex approached my office. His usual cocky demeanour was replaced with a reserved humility. He admitted to his past mistakes and presented a plan for his personal development. His self-awareness was admirable and his willingness to change was encouraging.

As he left my office, I was left alone with my thoughts. The decision I faced was no longer about just Alex, but about taking a chance on potential over reliability. It was a gamble by any measure, but isn't that what business is often about? Taking calculated risks in the hope of greater rewards?

In the end, I decided to give Alex the chance to prove himself. His display of maturity and self-awareness demonstrated the potential that we initially saw in him. It was a risk, but a risk I was willing to take. Perhaps, in the great scheme of things, this last chance was not just for Alex, but for me and my ability to look beyond his flaws and see a possible future leader in the company.

The rise of Bing in popularity, although astonishing, wasn’t a surprise to everyone. It became clear that Bing had managed to effectively tap into a market space that was slowly becoming disenchanted with Google's monopoly. However, as Bing's popularity peaked, there was an interesting twist in this search engine saga: the emergence of competitors like Yandex and DuckDuckGo.

Yandex, hailing from Russia, began to carve out a global presence. It offered services similar to Bing and Google, like mail, maps, and image search capabilities. What set it apart, however, was its ability to navigate the Cyrillic alphabet better than its competitors, which quickly made it a favorite among Russian users.

On the other hand, DuckDuckGo started to appeal to users who prioritized privacy over everything else. Unlike most search engines, it doesn't track user data for advertising, winning over users who didn't want their search history sold to the highest bidder.

As Bing made way for these players, it created a more nuanced, diversified search engine market. People were no longer limited to Google. They now had more choices, depending on what they valued most in a search engine: Bing's integration with Microsoft's suite, Yandex's Eastern European acumen, or DuckDuckGo’s unprecedented privacy policies.

While Bing’s climb in popularity opened the door for increased competition, it created an environment that fostered innovation. This move challenged the status quo of the search engine industry and proved that even in a market dominated by a powerful entity like Google, there was still room for choice, diversity and competition.

Continuing into the future, the landscape of search engine industry might see more shifts. New features, improved personalization, integration with other services, and increased user privacy could all become key factors in differentiating these companies. But for now, Bing's triumph and its subsequent move to create more competition have forged a path toward a more diverse and user-focused era of search. It has shown the tech industry that nothing is set in stone and that even giants can be rattled.

Pushing back my initial wave of panic, I knew I had to shift my focus onto the task at hand. This man could barely take an unassisted breath, his life hanging by a thread that was ominously thin. Death, the merciless robber, was rapidly trying to steal away the lively soul of this man.

I rushed forward, my hand reaching out for the defibrillator. A device that carried the weight of an individual's life in the pure kinetic energy generated by its circuits and wires. I looked back to the patriarch of this life, his eyes closed - eerily peaceful amidst the chaotic situation.

His son stood in the corner of the room, consumed by the helpless despair threatening to overpower him. His father's gasps from the brink of death echoed in his ears, amplifying his desperation. His pleas for help were drowned out by the cacophony of life-saving machines beeping and medical personnel who were busy in their choreographed attempt to ward off death.

"Charge to 200!" I ordered, my voice cutting through the tension-filled room. The sound of the defibrillator as it cranked up sent shivers down the spine of every present in the room. Paddles firmly connected to the dying man's chest, I looked up, hoping for a sign from above to tell me that everything would be alright.

"Clear!" I commanded, the room falling into an unwelcome silence as I delivered the first shock. His body jerked harshly in response, a shuddering gasp escaping his lips before he succumbed to the stillness once again.

"Again, charge to 250!" I moved my stare from the man's face to the monitor, which was displaying his vital signs in glaring red digits. His heartbeat was irregular to say the least, and dwindling by the second. 

With my heart pounding in my chest, I administered a second charge. Blood vessels pulsed violently beneath pale skin, as if fighting their own battle for survival within the man's body. 

Gradually, with every passing second, the shrill alarming tone of the heart monitor started to lose its erratic rhythm, slowly taking the shape of a steady, rhythmic throb.

Finally, with a sigh of relief, I looked at the son, my eyes meeting his, full of intimidations. "He's stable now," I told him, struggling to hide the triumphant spark in my eyes, "but he's not out of the woods yet."

I wouldn't let him die. I won't let him slip away.

Patterson, renowned for his pioneering work in the field of neurology. Despite having retired from active practice, he had agreed to consult on my father's case out of professional curiosity.

As our plane descended into Phoenix, the vast reddish-brown landscape stretched out in all directions. Towering cacti stood casting long shadows over the barren desert, seemingly mirroring our solitary quest for answers. The sinking sun painted the sky in hues of orange and pink, as if announcing our arrival to the land of healing.

At the Sky Harbor International Airport, we were met by Dr. Patterson's intern, a young woman named Lucy who had taken a few days off her busy schedule to assist us. She piled our luggage into her dusty off-roader, before steering us expertly through the early evening traffic to our accommodations.

The following morning, we found ourselves sitting in the office of the distinguished Dr. Patterson. His reputation preceded him, and yet there was nothing intimidating about his demeanor. Behind the gray hair and the horn-rimmed glasses, I could see a pair of kindly eyes, now trained on my father's MRI scans.

Over the course of the next week, we spent countless hours discussing the case, examining the test results, and exploring possible treatments. Dr. Patterson proved to be a reservoir of wisdom and compassion, diligently answering all our queries, even the easiest ones. He did not offer an instant magical solution, but what he promised was a carefully planned strategy based on years of experience.

Every night, we'd return to our hotel room armed with new knowledge and a glimmer of hope. Every morning, we'd set out to learn more, inspired by Dr. Patterson's unwavering dedication.

As we boarded our plane back home, two weeks later, we carried with us not just answers and a treatment plan, but also a newfound respect for the resilience of the human spirit. Our journey to Arizona had turned out to be just as much a lesson in faith and patience as it was in medicine. And in Dr. Patterson, we had found not just a brilliant doctor, but also a shining beacon of humanity.

I stretched out lazily on the bed, relishing in the warmth of the cozy blankets around me. The wonderful aroma of breakfast being cooked filled every corner of the small apartment, letting me know that today was going to be a good day. Through half-closed eyes, I glanced at the alarm clock on the bedside cabinet. It was only 7 in the morning. Early enough for the day to feel fresh and ripe with possibilities, yet late enough for me to enjoy a long, humane sleep.

Reluctant to leave the snugness of my bed, I decided to lay there a while longer, allowing my senses to fully wake up. The smell coming from the kitchen was intoxicating – it was the pleasant, homey scent of butter and eggs, and something else too. Could that be bacon?

I tossed the covers aside and strolled to the kitchen, tracing the source of the mouth-watering smells. Sunlight streamed through the windows, casting a beautiful beam across the living room, which remarkably accentuated the warm, golden hue of the wooden furniture.

Entering into the kitchen, I was greeted by the sight of my partner humming a cheery tune while expertly flipping a pancake high in the air. Freshly brewed coffee sat on the counter, its rich aroma mingling with the smell of cooked breakfast. It was a tradition we had since moving together – one would cook a surprise breakfast for the other on random days, a small gesture that added more sweetness to our relationship.

My partner turned around, a flash of surprise and an expanding grin on their face. "Good morning, sleepyhead," they greeted, planting a kiss on my forehead. 

"Good morning," I replied, my eyes still set on the sumptuous breakfast he cooked. The table was laden with a breakfast feast – scrambled eggs, crispy bacon, and an array of brightly colored fruits. 

I took my seat at the breakfast nook while my partner served both plates in front of us, a satisfied smile on their face. Breakfast tasted even better when cooked with love on a sunny morning. With every bite, I realized just how lucky I was to have this moment, to have my partner, and to have this sunny morning filled with butter, scrambled eggs, and a whole lot of love. Today was, indeed, going to be a good day.

His fingers throbbed slightly as he flexed them, a residual aftereffect from aggressively strumming the plastic guitar controller throughout the entire evening. The chorus of the last song they had played echoed in his half-drunken sleep, vivid bursts of neon colors from the game's display still imprinted behind his eyelids. His room was a disaster zone - discarded snack wrappers and empty cans of beer were strewn everywhere, mixed in with the tangled clump of wires and gaming accessories across the carpet.

The laughter of his friends, their cheering and occasional off-pitch singing during their haphazard attempts to score, all rang in his ears but was slowly beginning to fade away. His bed was warmer than he remembered it being, the comforting scent of his own cozily faded sheets lulling him into a heavier form of slumber.

Suddenly, the shrill sound of his cell phone's ringtone penetrated the semi-silence. Josh groaned and rolled over, fumbling on his side table through the darkness until he found it. His blurry eyes squinted to make out the incoming caller ID but failed. All effort exhausted, he brought the intrusive invader to his ear and grumbled a rough "Hello".

The voice on the other end was familiar, yet out-of-place in this time of quiet. It was Tommy, their so-called 'Rock Band' vocalist and one of Josh's long-time friends. His words were jumble - something about forgetting his jacket and keys at Josh's place.

Josh grumbled something unintelligible and told Tommy he would leave them in the mailbox for him to collect the next morning. After cutting the call, he began to drift back into his previous state, the boundaries between awake and asleep slowly blurring once again. Every now and again, the strumming pattern on the Rock Band guitar would flutter through his mind and he would relive a moment of that night's rock-n-roll fiesta.

Leaning back into his pillows, he closed his eyes and drifted off again. The quiet of the night was now occasionally punctuated by the distant hooting of the city buses and a faint urban hum. He could still picture the colored notes flying down the television screen, but they were gradually receding as slumber claimed him once more. The peaceful calm after the storm of their neighbor-disturbing jam session caressed him, accompanied sweetly by the soft sighing of the wind outside. The weighted fatigue draped over him like a comfy blanket. Josh knew no more Rock Band was to be played tonight.

The lords and ladies are the true power players in my kingdom, each one with a web of informers and free to spin their own version of the truth until reality is cloaked in half-truths and nimbly dodged lies. "Contrary to what has been said by rumor mongers, we are not at war with our neighbouring realm."

An incredulous murmur ripples through the crowd instantly. Their shocked faces suggest that I might as well have just declared the sky is red. 

I raise my hands, calling for silence. "This is not to say we're suddenly in league with them either. No, our relationship remains much the same. Our forces have exchanged blows at the border. We've lost men and so have they," I state, the hard truth causing a silence to devour the murmur.

"Yes, there are conflicts, and yes, these are challenging times. But do not mistake a few border skirmishes as a declaration of war." I pause, my eyes scanning the crowd. "This unrest is caused by fear. Fear leads to chaos. And chaos," I point at them, "chaos benefits none of us. Order and unity, these are what we need in such times."

A thin veil of silence drapes over the room. I hope my words have resonated with them. It is time to stop these rumors that are sowing discord in our realm. As the king, it's up to me to hold things together. I pray I've done my part today. "Remember, we are stronger together. Do your part to spread truth, not fear."

A cheer goes up from the crowd, echoing through the room. I've given them something to cling to in troubled times. As they disperse, I can only hope that my words reach far and wide, dispelling the destructive rumors that are threatening to fracture my kingdom.

Every night, as I walked home from work, I would pass the old man sitting on a faded blue bench in the park. He was like a fixture – an integral part of the landscape. His name was George, although he was mostly known as ‘Old George’ due to his advancing years and somewhat gnarled appearance. But there was a certain charm about him, a particular sparkle in his grey-blue eyes that spoke volumes about the life he had led.

Every evening, without fail, I would find him in the same spot, hunched over a wood-carved chessboard. The pieces, worn and chipped due to years of use, would be meticulously arranged, ready for an enigmatic competitor. His hands, wrinkled and quaking slightly from years of toil and hardship, would move his pieces with utmost care and precision.

Sometimes, he played against some passersby, and other times, an unseen and anticipated opponent that could only be his lively imagination. An empty chair sat across him, its vacancy almost echoing a quiet invitation to any passerby. "Care to play a game?" the empty chair seemed to silently ask.

George frequently spoke about his younger days - his days as a Princeton graduate, his passion for mathematics, his stint in Navy during the war, his years as a prolific chess player, and his lovely wife, Andrea, who had passed away many years before. Each tale was rich, steeped in layers of wisdom and sentimentality.

His love for the game of chess never withered. Instead, it seemed to flourish with each passing day. He claimed it kept his mind sharp, his spirit robust. When asked if he ever grew tired of it, his response was the same. "Chess is like life, kid," he would say with a wise smile, "unpredictable, challenging, and requires lots of strategizing. Also, it's full of surprises. Each day brings a new game, a new challenge, just like life."

Despite his age and solitude, George never seemed lonely. He had his chess game and the ever-changing, yet ever the same park, which became his home ground. He brought a sense of continuity in a world that was spinning too fast, a sense of an unwavering faith in a world that was constantly evolving.

My evening walks home somehow always felt richer after encountering George. His tales, his wisdom, his passion for the game, all left me with a feeling of enduring hope. In him, it was always the same game, but yet somehow, it was different each day.

Shadows played on its green surface, swirled around by the dim overhead lights that cast a foreboding glow. The room was silent, the stale scent of cigar smoke lingering in the air, a relic from past games, past bids, past laughs, and past desperation.

The young man, long fingers traced the black outlines of the spades, diamonds, hearts, and clubs printed onto the felt, trying to draw courage from every fiber. There were years of stories etched into this table.

His heart pounded heavily, adrenaline coursing through his veins, amplifying the tension that had fallen upon the room. The room fell into a deeper silence. His reputation preceded him: ruthless, unpredictable, and with a killer poker face that could make the most seasoned players crumble. Tonight, he was the enemy. Tonight, the young man had to beat him, to prove himself in this underworld of high stakes poker.

With a dizzying rush, blurred images swirled around me; a collage of time - of then, now, and beyond - and suddenly, I was standing amidst a bustling marketplace, under a sign reading: "Yorkshire, 1936." In the absolute silence of my room, the pendulum tick-tocking relentlessly, I began to understand the magnitude of my power. And so, I venture on, a silent guardian of time, keeping its secrets, reveling in its mysteries, and respecting its power. "To be original is the ultimate challenge," my mentor often said, but I detested that line. The notion of originality made it seem like everything great had already been done, and this left no room for those of us struggling to make our mark on the world. His words began to chip away at my enthusiasm. When cerebral sparks for what I believed were revolutionary ideas ignited in my mind, they were immediately extinguished by that infamous phrase.

"It's been done before," he would state bluntly, a dismissive wave of his hand rendering my ideas worthless. It became a mantra that echoed in my ears, seeping deeply into my psyche. It critically undermined my confidence, my passion began to flail, every creative nerve begging for mercy.

The words became a beast I wrestled with every day. It grew, feeding off my insecurity, snarling at my attempts to appease it with innovative ideas. I fell victim to the discouragement, productivity strangled by a shadow of self-doubt. The passion that once coursed through me with vigor was now the feeble flicker of a single candle struggling against a tempest.

One evening, while marinated in frustration, I decided to take a different approach. If everything had been done before, it was time to stop trying to be entirely original and instead lend a new perspective to the existing world, to the already done. I set out to improve, innovate, and redefine.

And so, I began to experiment, stripping away everything I had learned, breaking down concepts, techniques, and ideas into their most basic forms. I examined them with a fresh pair of eyes, unfettered by prejudice or preconceptions. Refusing to be limited by what was 'done,' I embarked on a journey of exploration, of curiosity, and ultimately, of self-realization.

I discovered that there was beauty in reshaping the conventional, in challenging the usual, as long as it was backed with intention and meaning. The obsession with uniqueness, I realized, was a trap. Instead, it was the pursuit of understanding and meaningful creation that held true value.

Armed with this new-found conviction, I emerged from the shadows of the beast. My creations, while not entirely new in the most literal sense, carried the indelible stamp of my perspectives and the depth of my understanding.

Now, when I hear the phrase, "It's been done before," all it brings out of me is a healthy chuckle, laden with the wisdom of my previous struggles. It's a friendly reminder of the transformation in my ethos—a journey from despair to self-assuredness. Please, let those words come; they now harbor no fear but only fuel the fire of my individuality. The beast within had been tamed, and it was now a wellspring of inspiration. Yes, it's indeed been done before, but never my way.

In the end, it was not about being original, but about being authentic. It was about pouring heart and soul into my work, making it unabashedly mine and adding value in my unique way. I stop striving for originality and start embodying my authenticity, creating a beautiful amalgamation of the old and new with a flair distinctly mine, distinctly unique.

After Famine, their sights were set on Pestilence. The town had been prepared for this. The community built, repaired, and worked tirelessly to secure the town against Pestilence's plagues. 

Pestilence, much like Famine, didn't seem all that intimidating at first. He was an old, haggard man with a fragile body that would falter with a strong gust of wind. Yet when he did arrive at the town, his emaciated, sallow form concealed a deadly potency. As soon as he came, the first people fell. 

Still, they fought, armed with herbs, sanitization, and their most vital weapon – determination. It felt like nature was hell-bent on wiping them out, a weak colony of humans in a desolate wasteland. But they stood their ground, tending to one another, banding together like a close-knit family.

They fell, one by one, adding to the growing pile of bodies against which they waged their war. Pestilence’s hideous laugh echoed through the air, signaling another soul claimed. 

But the townsfolk didn't fall apart. A compassion, unity, and determination spread through them, more infectious than the plague Pestilence brought. They managed to isolate the sick, treated them with tried and tested herbal remedies, and burnt the bodies – an act of respect for the fallen and a strategic move against spreading the infection. 

Eventually, their ceaseless trials paid off. With every lost member, their resolve hardened, and soon the echoes of Pestilence’s laughter dwindled. The weak and frail man succumbed to the very plague he'd intended for them.

With Pestilence vanquished, they were left with two more Horsemen– War and Death. The colony was already reeling from the blows of Famine and Pestilence. Dealing with War and Death seemed insurmountable, a daunting challenge almost beyond their reach. Yet, they'd come this far, survived the unfathomable. They couldn't falter now. It was time to prepare again, to rally their defenses and brace themselves for confronting the last two Horsemen.
